name: Athena
summary: A frontline Guardian who sacrifices her own health to generate massive shields and {taunt} enemies using [Martial Verdict]. She excels at protecting vulnerable allies by redirecting their incoming damage to herself with {life_link}. Additionally, she provides heavy area-of-effect retaliation through [Counter Helix], whose cooldown is removed once she enters the {wild} state.
title: Goddess of Wisdom
lore:
The goddess of wisdom and war from Olympus, daughter of Zeus. The owl that follows her serves as both symbol and messenger. Graceful and radiant, she is said to have taught humanity countless crafts, watching over every aspect of their lives. In war, she guides them to victory—in peace, she safeguards order, even helping lay the foundations of law in the mortal realm.

"Wisdom leads to victory. Order brings prosperity."

Though she watches over the fate of all humankind, she does not interfere in the course of individual destinies, nor does she involve herself deeply in mortal lives. Instead, she hopes humanity will find the strength to overcome danger and disaster on their own. Thus, she rarely strikes directly against the demons and monsters of the world—instead offering guidance to the brave, and heroes like Perseus, Jason, and Odysseus once followed her divine prophecies.

"Knowledge may be taught by others, but fate must be grasped by one's own hand."

According to prophecy, Athena was destined to become a goddess so mighty she would one day surpass Zeus himself. Fearing her birth, Zeus swallowed her mother whole—yet this act only sealed his fate. Within his skull, Athena grew, drawing divine power from the king of gods. When the agony of his headache became unbearable, Zeus ordered Hephaestus to split his head open with an axe. From within sprang the goddess of war, fully armored, shield and spear in hand—her cry as fierce as her wisdom was boundless.

"My birth heralds the flame of wisdom, cast forth upon the world."

Stern by nature, she shows no mercy to those who defy her divine authority. She honors her father deeply and has never overstepped her bounds, standing as a guardian of order on Olympus. When Hades, long resentful, stirred up strife among the gods, she dutifully delivered punishment. Yet Zeus, fearful of prophecy, remains wary—always watching her from a distance. When the Ring of Dominion called, she answered in the name of justice, crossing into another world to aid in the battle against Ladon.

Athena attempted to imprison Hades in Tartarus, but the Lord of the Underworld, with the help of the Wild Hunt, grew stronger and instead imprisoned her. However, the Goddess of Wisdom did not submit. She thought of the Ringsworn Legion, who also stood on the side of light. Although she eventually escaped, the chaos in space-time remained unresolved, and a catastrophe involving countless worlds loomed on the horizon. Meanwhile, the situation on the Olympus side was also turbulent, with the scheming Zeus planning a new uprising...

name: Prometheus
summary: A stat-stealing Guardian who suppresses enemy Critical Damage and converts stolen power into exceptional self-sustain. [Nebula Chains] drains a target's combat stats while restoring a large amount of HP and all of her Rage, and her follow-up attacks generate stacking shields. In the {wild} state, [Cross Chain Strike] gains full Lifesteal and [Triple Spiral] benefits from {awakening} without consuming its stacks.
title: Firethief Goddess
lore: Prometheus is one of the Titans, renowned for the feat of creating humanity and stealing heavenly fire. As a seer, she molded humans from clay and endowed them with spirit, always playing the role of a guardian of humanity. In defiance of Zeus's will to treat humans as puppets, she stole fire and delivered it to the human world, angering the King of the Gods, and was eternally bound to the Caucasus cliffs to endure the daily torment of having her liver pecked. She is a symbol of the enlightenment of civilization.

Prometheus embodies both keen intellect and far-reaching foresight. When Zeus decreed that humankind must offer him the finest cuts of meat in sacrifice, the people turned to her for counsel. At her urging, they concealed the choicest portions of beef beneath the entrails, while arranging gleaming fat over bare bones. Deceived by appearances, Zeus chose the bones, leaving the true bounty to humanity. This stratagem not only shaped the tradition of human sacrifice thereafter, but also revealed her gift for turning the rules of power against themselves to safeguard the weak. That same cunning brilliance would later find even bolder expression in her plan to steal fire.

When Zeus deprived humanity of the right to use fire to suppress the development of civilization, Prometheus chose to break a fennel branch to steal the spark, granting humanity the ability to illuminate the darkness, forge metal, and cook food. She knew well that Zeus would inevitably deliver harsh punishment once he learned the truth, yet she persisted in helping the weak. Indeed, after discovering the truth, Zeus chained her to the Caucasus Mountains and sent an eagle to peck at her innards—day after day...

After being rescued by Heracles, Prometheus was freed from physical torment, yet she came to grasp more deeply the bond between divinity and humankind. She continued to guide the age of heroes from the shadows—directing Heracles toward the completion of his Twelve Labors and aiding Jason in the pursuit of the Golden Fleece. From these trials emerged a truth that reached beyond myth: a true prophet does not bow to the decrees of fate, but kindles the fire of hope amid despair.

Upon entering the realm of Phantasia Mountain, Prometheus witnessed the countless possibilities of this new world. Amid the strife of battling gods, humanity still struggled between monster and divinity. The eternal fire-bearer lifted her gaze once more—vowing to guard the spark of thought and continuity for whatever new civilization may rise from the chaos.
quote: Passing down fire is my mission.
ssr_quote: Is this flame a hope or a curse?

title: Judge of the Underworld
lore:
Anubis, god of death, is the son of the desert god Set and his wife Nephthys. He oversees the rites of mummification and guides the souls of the dead to their judgment. Though silent in form, his presence marks the endless rhythm of life, death, and all that lies between.

"Life and death, an endless cycle."

Anubis was once the guardian of tombs and a master of embalming. His body is depicted as black—symbolizing rebirth, life, and the fertile soil of the Nile, as well as the darkened hue of a body preserved through mummification.

After Osiris's body was torn into fourteen pieces and scattered, Isis painstakingly gathered each fragment. Anubis, guardian of the dead, aided her in reuniting the flesh, wrapping the remains in sacred linens. Thus, the first mummy was born—an act that forever bound death to ritual, and sorrow to reverence.

During the ritual of soul judgment, Anubis holds the scales—one side bearing the heart of the deceased, the other a feather from Ma'at, goddess of truth. Only a heart lighter than, or equal in weight to, the feather may pass into the afterlife.

"All pray for the next life—but it is their own deeds that decide if they reach it."
Anubis handed the position of Lord of the Underworld to Osiris. Now, he stands watch over the mountains and the lands of preservation, guiding each soul to judgment and the afterlife.

title: Triumphant Princess
combat_tags: High Physical Defense and Magic Defense
lore: Caesar Nibelungen is the eldest daughter of Constantine XI, the Crown Princess, and the heir to the Nibelgard Empire. As a member of the imperial family, she grew up under relentless study and training. Even in her youth, Caesar was aware of the doubts surrounding her as a female heir, with only her father firmly supporting her claim as Crown Princess. To repay this trust, she pushed herself far beyond ordinary limits to earn recognition and support, gradually becoming a leader the people were willing to follow to the very end.

The Nibelungen family claims descent from Vidofnir, the Eagle of Light, and has ruled the empire for centuries. Yet their bloodline is plagued by a hereditary affliction known as the Madwyrm Plague. Those afflicted undergo draconification, growing scales, descending into madness, and eventually losing their human form. Legend says the curse began when the empire's founder consumed a dragon's heart. Symptoms manifest in all Nibelungen descendants as they age.

"Those who fight dragons too long will see their offspring become dragons." — History Since the Founding of the Empire

As the Madwyrm Plague worsened, Constantine XI's paranoia spread even to his most trusted daughter. At the annual ceremony, the cheers for the princess drowned out those for the emperor. Exploited by court jesters, the princess was lured from the capital with rumors of a cure beyond the borders.

While Caesar was campaigning abroad, the ambitious imperial general Pompey incited rebellion within the empire and framed the princess for treason. Having lost her beloved father and been stripped of all authority, Caesar became a traitor with nowhere to belong. Exiled, she made contact with the emperor's loyal minister Crassus, only to be betrayed by her own subordinates and captured. With Crassus's support, she was rescued by the Silver Eagle Knights, and with their aid began the long road to reclaim her empire, opening the first chapter of legend.

After defeating the rebel Pompey and reclaiming her rightful throne, she prepared to fully wield her power, ushering in an era that belonged to her.

"Word from the capital suggests that under the new emperor's rule, this age will be remembered as a golden era that left countless hearts sighing." — The Decline of Nibelgaard
ssr_quote: I came, I saw, I conquered.

title: Flameforged Dragon Princess
lore: As the divinely appointed Guardian, Dvalinn has borne the responsibility of sustaining the vitality of the Nine Realms since ancient times. She is granted authority over flame and forging and commands the valiant Red Dragon Legion.

After the first Twilight, the gods perished. With divine suppression gone, demons and calamities returned to the world. Dvalinn led the Red Dragon Legion in honoring the ancient oath, continuing to guard the Nine Realms.
The anvil is her war drum. The forge is her heart. Dvalinn protects life with steel and flame, forging weapons for the Red Dragon Legion that even demons fear.

Despite fallen companions, fading kin, and the loss of divine power, Dvalinn and her legion never leave the front lines against catastrophe. She believes that the survival of countless lives outweighs any individual glory.

Today, Dvalinn's name is spoken among all living beings, a symbol of courage, resilience, and hope. Some say she still soars high above the skies, watching every corner of the world with a piercing gaze, ever ready for the battles yet to come.

name: Heidrun
summary: A shield-focused Guardian who supports ranged and Otherworld Return allies through {deathrattle} effects. Her active damage builds shields, while [Mirror Judicator] grants Deathrattle to allies and converts her own HP into further protection. She also dispels enemy buffs, summons phantoms in the {wild} state, and restores Rage to Wild Spirit allies with [Guardian Sweep].
title: Heroic Soul Commander
combat_tags: Buff Dispel and Judgment of the Magic Ring
lore:
Heidrun, one of the ancient nature spirits of the Nine Realms, is renowned for her unwavering HP. She feeds on the tender leaves of the World Tree, Yggdrasill, and was personally chosen by the All-Father Odin to oversee the training of all Heroic Warriors in Valhalla.
Through Targeted Teaching, she either reveals a Warrior's hidden weaknesses, forcing them to temper themselves into steel, or provides precise guidance to hone their combat skills. With the clarity and resilience of a nature spirit, she forges each Heroic Warrior into a Champion capable of facing despair and charging into the battlegrounds of Ragnarok.

“Heidrun stands on Valhalla’s roof, nibbling on the branches of Lærad. From her horns flows mead, filling the great vat till it overflows every day, quenching the thirst of all the Heroic Warriors.” — Edda Manuscript: Grimnir’s Sayings

In the hearts of countless Warriors in the Hall of Heroes, some revere her as the strictest Mentor, for she can pierce through their deepest, hidden weaknesses with a single glance and strike directly at the core with unmatched sharpness. Others respect her as a nurturing Mentor, patiently guiding their Path of Ascension and preparing lavish meals and fine mead for the Warriors returning from Crimson Onslaught.
What she aims to teach the Warriors is never just an invincible Strength but also the understanding that behind this pursuit of power lies a purpose worth guarding with their lives.

“All Heroic Warriors who drink that mead are reborn anew each day after battle, until the horn of Ragnarok is sounded.” —Edda Manuscript『Prose Edda: Gullveig's Deception』

Heidrun upholds the principle of properly guiding every Heroic Warrior in the Hall of Heroes, with an almost obsessive dedication to ensuring that every Warrior around her receives instruction. Upon learning of the fate of Ragnarok, all of Asgard was thrown into chaos, but it was the Heroic Warriors in the Hall of Heroes who, under Heidrun's guidance, maintained their fighting spirit. The Warriors remember why they entered the Hall of Heroes in the first place, and their training roars cause the World Tree to tremble.

“Before the end of days comes, her mead will never run dry, and the Heroic Warriors' valor will never fade.” —The Poetic Edda: The Seeress's Prophecy

In the apocalyptic battle that engulfed the Nine Realms in flames, the golden hall of Asgard collapsed with a thunderous crash. Countless gods and Heroic Warriors fell in battle. Heidrun, leading the remaining Heroic Warriors, fought valiantly in a Crimson Onslaught, yet was unable to avert the inevitable fate.
As Twilight descended, the Nine Realms turned to scorched earth, and she became one of the few survivors. She returned to the ruins of Asgard and sang requiems for each fallen Warrior. They all followed her teachings, fighting until their very last moment of life, for it was the ultimate Glory Days of the fearless. Yet, as the final note of the requiem faded into the charred wind, Heidrun ultimately let fall scalding tears.

After Ragnarok, Heidrun wandered through the ruins of the Nine Realms, eventually arriving at Phantasia Mountain. Here gathered battle-slain heroes, lost souls, and shards left behind by the fallen gods—no longer distinguished by identity, only united as fellow travelers crushed by fate.
Heidrun's current goal is no longer to cultivate invincible warriors but to help every soul broken by fate rise again. She wields truth as her sword and companionship as her shield, guiding every lost soul to find the Courage to take the first step toward the mountain summit amidst the pain of being seen through and the warmth of acceptance.

name: Helveil
summary: A regenerating Guardian who creates a powerful Shield Formation using [Spirit Shackles], granting herself immense Damage Reduction and crowd control immunity. She sustains herself by absorbing enemy souls with [Soul Suck] and passively healing from non-critical hits through her [Soul Domain]. As allies fall, she gains {deathrattle} stacks, further increasing her Critical Resistance.
title: Fallen Warborn Goddess
lore:
Once a Warborn Goddess of Valhalla, she turned her back on the path of light and joined the ranks of the Wild Hunt. Deception is her delight, and she often takes the form of a radiant Warborn Goddess to lure brave souls to their doom. Obsessed with the thrill of battle, she fights with a ferocity more beast than warrior. It's said she even once tore off one of her own wings in a fit of frenzy...

"To be lost is to be free. To fall... is to be unbound."

Unlike other Warborn Goddesses, she is not a daughter of Odin, but a descendant of Berserkers. Born among mortals, she disguised herself as a boy from a young age, boarding a pirate ship in search of a lost magical sword and embarking on a life of adventure. Upon claiming the divine blade, she earned Odin's recognition, and after death, her soul was transformed into a Warborn Goddess. At first, she served in Valhalla with faith in Odin and devotion to courage and justice—guiding lost souls toward their path. And yet...

After witnessing her descendants die one after another due to the curse of the demon sword, grief consumed her. Only then did she realize that Odin had used her and her kin—sacrificing them all for the sake of safely claiming the blade. Betrayed by the gods she once revered, her faith shattered. Resentment festered, and over years of quiet anguish, her mind began to unravel. At last, she orchestrated a masterful betrayal—one that dealt a devastating blow to Valhalla itself.

In her madness, she forged a new faith—one of darkness and destruction—and formed a secret pact with Hel, goddess of death. Now she roams the world, harvesting souls while evading the pursuit of her former Warborn Goddess sisters. To mock the weakness of Valhalla, she often takes on the guise of an ordinary Warborn Goddess, tricking others into aiding her soul-gathering, sullying their names in the process.

"Here's the cold, hard truth—the Warborn Goddesses you worship are nothing but liars and frauds."

She actively sought out the Black Knight, offering to help bring about a second Ragnarok. She revealed many of Valhalla's secrets and unleashed legendary horrors upon the world. As long as she can take revenge on the gods, no act is too wicked, no price too high.

"In a world built on lies, only destruction is true salvation!"

title: Ironclad Commander
lore: A general of the Nibelgard Empire, known for commanding vast armies and quelling unrest with swift, uncompromising force—striking without hesitation, whether facing threats within or beyond the empire's borders.

When the endless army appeared across the wasteland, the barbarian scout's bone whistle froze in his throat, and the chieftain could hear his curved blade weeping in its sheath. Beside the imperial general, the war banners snapped in the wind as thundering hooves shook the earth.

Her battle boots were stained with blood for the first time at the age of twelve during the autumn hunting festival. While other noble girls were still practicing their manners in the court, a blood-stained roe deer had already fallen to her precise archery. On the night she refused a marriage proposal at seventeen, she smashed the jade bracelet sent by the suitor, smearing the blood beads from her fingertip on the letter of rejection. Ultimately, the imperial military academy she aspired to join made an exception to admit this noble girl.

Smoke from the border fires blackened the city walls. She remembers the silk ribbon on her saddle, stiff with dried blood. The wind slammed ash from burning granaries into her face, mingled with the taste of iron rising in her throat—like swallowing the shattered blades of a battlefield. When the barbarians' horn sounded again, she remembered it. And she vowed to forever hunt down that discordant sound that shattered the empire's peace.

"Seriously?! Those drunkards must have crud for brains?! Make peace with the barbarians? Hah!" She tore the emperor's order to retreat into shreds and had the royal messenger executed on the spot.
"The emperor has fallen under the sway of traitors. Soldiers of the empire—our target is the capital! March! Purge the throne!"

name: Salome

[Stormdance of the Sands] grants a shield and applies {shock}, while [Drunken Phantom Dance] raises allied Dodge and can {charm} enemies after enough Drunken Step Aroma has accumulated. Her Overdrive greatly increases her own Dodge and becomes more powerful as those Aroma stacks grow.
title: Dancer of Seven Veils
lore: Salome grew up in the depths of a court intertwined with power and intrigue, witnessing the darkest aspects of the mortal world from a young age. Her mother groomed her into the sharpest weapon, with unparalleled beauty and mesmerizing dance as the sheath that concealed her edge. Whenever her mother drove her with love, she could fulfill her mother's wishes, even if it meant taking another's life. Her mother was undoubtedly satisfied and proud, but poor Salome could no longer discern the boundary between love and death.

More and more people are drawn to Salome's beauty and her dance. To win her favor, they prove willing to grant nearly any request she makes. Some bring her jewels beyond price; others scour the world for legendary curiosities and exotic beasts. There are even those who lay their dignity at her feet, offering themselves up for her amusement. Her mother, too, comes to realize that Salome is slipping beyond her control. Seeking Salome's protection, she finds herself reduced to the same bargain—pleasing her daughter in exchange for shelter. Salome, for her part, gives this fragile, desperate devotion a single name: "love."

Salome could not endure the sting of unreturned devotion or the humiliation of refusal. To her, love was never a matter of shared warmth—it was an absolute craving, one that demanded total fulfillment and complete possession, even if such possession led the beloved to ruin. The love she offered and the love she claimed to receive were tested and affirmed again and again in ever more extravagant displays. From that point on, her joy became inseparable from this fevered notion of "love," until at last she was wholly enslaved by her own desire.

Salome no longer cared whether the object of her "love" was her mother, a suitor, or any figure of power she might bend to her will. Every dance, every demand, became a cruel rite—a test in which the other must surrender what they treasured most to prove the "purity" and "intensity" of their devotion. To her, destruction was the ultimate form of possession, and suffering the surest proof of loyalty. And in this dark creed, Salome willingly drowned.

When her mother pleaded for the removal of the final obstacle to her ascension as queen, Salome agreed without hesitation.
At the feast, her dance became both coronation offering and final challenge to the prophet.
When it ended, she spoke plainly: "Bring me the head of John on a silver platter." When the platter was set before her, she gazed upon its burden and felt a double fulfillment. Her mother's "love" was fixed forever in fear and gratitude, and the prophet's "love" was claimed in its most absolute form. This was Salome's ultimate trial—and all, in their own way, passed.
quote: If I can't have it, I'll destroy it all!
ssr_quote: Don't you want to admire my dance?

name: Xuanwu
summary: A shield-focused Guardian who layers [Mystic Sun] and [Mystic Moon] stacks through [Shifting Harmony] to grant allies passive Damage Reduction whenever shielded units are attacked by debuffed enemies. She enters [Divine Gift] during [Mortal Veil] to extend shielding across all allied Luminaries and Wyrms, dealing AoE damage scaled to her own shield value while remaining immune to control effects. [Mystic Beacon] supplements the team with targeted shields and [Haste], growing more powerful with each ally Overdrive through {awakening} stacks.
title: Four Saints
lore: Xuanwu, essence of the seven northern constellations and incarnation of lunar water virtue, bears the twin form of tortoise and serpent. Numbered among the Four Divine Beasts, Xuanwu holds dominion over the north, presides over the Dark Heavens, and cuts down demons and wicked spirits across the world.

Xuanwu is bold and free-spirited, with a deep love of wine. A wine gourd hangs at her waist year-round, and most people assume it holds the prized brews she has carefully collected. In truth, the gourd serves another purpose. She seals the fiends and demons she subdues within it. Those who can be reformed are granted freedom, while those who refuse to repent remain imprisoned inside, where they are distilled into wine. This special wine is known as Evil-Purging Brew.

When the hundred scourges stir in spring and summer, Xuanwu takes the form of a wandering hero, roaming the land to uphold good and vanquish evil. When they retreat into hiding in autumn and winter, Xuanwu resumes her identity as the Divine Lord and performs divinations for all under heaven at the year's end.
She drinks with the Azure Dragon at the turn from winter to spring, celebrating another year's safe passage.

Xuanwu's divinations never fail, but she rarely dares to perform them anymore. In her early years, while wandering the land, a few careless predictions of hers came true and drew countless people in pursuit of her. For a long time, Xuanwu had to evade these zealous followers, retreating more than once into remote mountains where few had ever set foot. By accident, she gave rise to many legends of mountain immortals. Plenty of others also used her name to make money, and over time, truth and rumor became impossible to tell apart.

Through divination, she learned that the other three Saints had already arrived at Phantasia Mountain. Following their trail, Xuanwu made her way there as well. Here, no one knows her name, and to her surprise, the divination signs that had never failed her suddenly stopped working. Now, she seeks only to find the source of this uncertainty—and discover who, or what, has broken the shackles of fate!

He supports his team by providing a widespread shield through [Nature's Embrace] and regenerating shielded allies.
title: Ancient Tree Guardian
lore: For a very long time, the treant Drasill lay in slumber—long enough for vines and mushrooms to sprout all over his bark. He's been awake for a while now, but it's never occurred to him to clean any of it off...

Drasill is the guardian of Nornwood Arbortide—kind-hearted and humble in daily life, always treating others with warmth. But when the forest is threatened by outsiders, his fury is swift and overwhelming, leaving intruders with no time for regret.

Drasill has lived for a very, very long time—and with his rather spotty memory, he no longer recalls how he first came into being. According to Drasill himself, by the time he became aware of anything at all, he'd already spent ages dwelling deep within the Nornwood.

The World Tree that supports all realms is called "Yggdrasill"—its name meaning "Odin's steed," with "drasill" meaning "horse" and Ygg being one of Odin's many names. A treant bearing a similar name, Drasill, may well be connected to Odin and the World Tree itself... but if so, he has long since forgotten.

With Phantasia Mountain in chaos, even the slow-witted Drasill has realized that a great disaster is brewing. Staying in the forest will no longer be enough to stay safe. So, the treant set out to find the Ringsworn—hoping to lend a branch of aid.

"Helping you is helping the forest!"

title: Ancient Golem
lore: A stone colossus often found in ancient ruins. Most of the time, it lies dormant, indistinguishable from an ordinary boulder. But the moment an enemy draws near, it rises from the earth and swings its massive stone fists with crushing force.

Adventurers speak in hushed tones of a supreme treasure hidden deep within the ruins guarded by a Goren. Some believe it grants wealth beyond imagination, others claim it can crown a king. But all who have sought it met the same fate—crushed beneath the Goren's stone fists.

Goren, as a rock colossus, is not a natural life form but a creation forged by mortal hands. Legend tells of a king from a distant age, a miser so obsessed with wealth that he would sooner see his kingdom fall to ruin than allow a single coin from his treasure hoard to be touched. To this end, he created Goren, entrusting him with the eternal vigil over a kingdom now crumbled to dust.

Some mages believe Goren was born of magical experiments. Just as the gods shaped humans from clay, so too did mortals imitate the divine—fashioning Goren from stone. The gods saw this as a violation of their sacred dominion, and in response, delivered a heavenly punishment that reduced the kingdoms of man to ruin.

While exploring ruins, the Ringsworn and their companions encountered Goren—and a battle broke out. Living up to their reputation, the party ultimately triumphed, but spared the golem's life. Curious about this whole "mercy" idea, the golem chose to follow them, eager to observe.
ssr_quote: Want to arm wrestle with me?

title: Slime King
lore:
Bouncy, squishy, and found just about everywhere, slimes are often dismissed as harmless grinding fodder for rookie adventurers. But if that's all you think they are, you're in for a rude awakening... Before you stands no ordinary blob—behold the Slime of all Slimes, the King of Kings, the eternal pinnacle of video game monsters—Gudong!!!

"Glooble?"

Its massive body is formed from the devoured remains of countless fellow slimes—making it, in a way, the product of a brutal bout of cannibalistic survival. Far stronger than any ordinary slime, and far heavier too... watch your step, or you might just get flattened!

Our king is wise! Our king is mighty! ...Well, in truth, his intellect doesn't quite surpass that of a common slime. So you'd best watch yourselves, humans—don't go plotting any clever tricks! To deceive the king is treason!

"Glooble, gloob!"

The coronation of the Slime King took place at high noon, beneath a blazing sun. Every slime in the forest gathered for the grand event. With great effort, the Slime King dragged his massive body forward, somehow producing a crown and royal skin from parts unknown, and bounced onto the podium to deliver his speech—only to find his subjects had already melted into puddles under the heat.

"Next time... let's do this on a cloudy day, okay?"

The Slime King usually rules over a vast underground kingdom—at least, that's how the slimes see it. Legend has it that tens of thousands of slimes live here, enough to draw the attention of curious adventurers. Some even gave these raids a name: Slime Showdown! In response, the Slime King raised the banner of resistance—or at least tried to. After all, he dreams of being the most feared creature on all of Phantasia Mountain.

name: Herman
summary: A savage Guardian who capitalizes on ally Overdrives to gain {awakening} stacks, unleashing continuous Spirit Flames that deal area damage and heal her. She disrupts enemies by applying {healing_down} and increasing their Overdrive costs with [Axe Boomerang]. She mitigates incoming non-Overdrive damage passively through [Fearless Iron Bulwark].
title: King of Beasts
lore:
This barbarian leader, the daughter of the Fenris tribe's chieftain, was sent to the Nibelgard Empire as a hostage after their rebellion failed. Recognized for her exceptional prowess, she was later recruited into the imperial army.

"To forget is to betray... Fenris will never be enslaved!"

Herman showed the unwavering obedience of a devoted servant to the Empire, stepping onto the battlefield for the first time already bearing the rank of Centurion. She did not disappoint—rising to prominence across numerous campaigns, and eventually earning both Imperial citizenship and a noble title.

"Oh, absolutely! I'm deeply honored to serve the Empire. It's just glorious!"

However, in reality, Herman never forgot that she was a descendant of the Beast Spirits, a member of the Fenris known as the "Barbarians," always waiting for a chance to avenge the Empire. She secretly contacted various Barbarian tribes and prepared a Raid against the Empire. 

"By the Beast Spirits! My bravest warriors—stand as one! Let the shameless Empire answer for its years of tyranny and conquest!"

Once all was in place, Herman exploited the Empire’s trust in her to lure the stationed Imperial Legion into the encirclement of the barbarian coalition. Amid dense forests and treacherous, mud-choked paths, the once-invincible legion was harried without end—until, under Herman’s command, it was utterly destroyed.

"Some fled. Others gathered in a last, desperate stand. At the edge of the bones lay shattered javelins... and the torn limbs of horses." — Chronicles of the Nilfgaard Empire

The Empire's frenzied counterattack exceeded even the worst expectations. Despite having Herman, who is well-versed in Imperial tactics, at the helm, the barbarian coalition continued to suffer defeat after defeat. Just when all seemed lost, an unexpected figure extended an olive branch for cooperation. 

"Listen up, Imperial scum, we're only teaming up temporarily. We'll settle the score with your bastard emperor father later."
quote: Spirit of the Beast, fight by my side!

title: Midsummer Night's Dreamer
lore:
Daughter of the Elf King and commander of the forest-dwelling elves, she leads with discipline and an unwavering sense of duty. Stern, precise, and rarely seen smiling, she insists on fighting at the front lines herself—personally defending the peace of the forest she calls home.

"Those who trespass in the forest... shall not be forgiven!"

Deeply devoted to her homeland, she thanks the forest aloud each time she gathers its fruits and quietly tends to injured animals in need. Though not one for words, her reverence and dedication to the forest are clear to all. Trusted by the elves and followed with respect, she devotes herself fully to the task of protecting the woodland she calls home. As an elven leader, she regards humans with the pride befitting her station.

Once, the free-spirited Flamefiend set the forest ablaze for her own amusement, and the ensuing fire destroyed the elves' homeland. Though guilt and sorrow weighed heavily on her heart, she wore no grief upon her face. Instead, with quiet resolve, she led her people to plant anew. Years passed. The forest returned, lush and alive once more—echoing once again with elven laughter beneath the green canopy.

She has long blamed herself for the catastrophe of years past, and her cold, exacting manner reflects that burden. Any change that might threaten the forest's safety is met with zero tolerance. Though she harbors deep hatred for the Flamefiend, she has suppressed her rage for years—for the sake of her people, and to prevent further bloodshed.

"I will give everything I have to the forest."

To better defend the forest, she sought ways to grow stronger—training tirelessly, learning to resonate with the forest's elements and spirits. Over the years, her magic deepened, and she earned victory after hard-won victory.

"This body is a shield to block the storm, a spear to clear the way."

title: Wild Outlaw
lore: A one-horned centaur with two horns. Technically. One of them is broken, but it doesn't slow him down in the slightest. He roams the grasslands of Phantasia Mountain at full gallop, charging wildly in whichever direction he pleases. Needless to say, don't expect him to follow any kind of speed limit.

The centaur race was born from the impious union between Ixion, King of the Lapiths, and the nymph Nephele—a blasphemy that drew the curse of the gods. As a result, all centaurs are born lacking self-restraint, often consumed by the pursuit of their own desires. Eurytion is no exception.

Eurytion once attended the wedding of his half-brother, Pirithous, king of the Lapiths—but drank himself into a stupor at the feast. In a drunken frenzy, he attempted to seize the bride for himself. Shamed and pursued for his disgraceful act, Eurytion fled to Phantasia Mountain, seeking refuge from the wrath that followed.
The name Eurytion means "flowing wine"—a nod to his love of drink and a foreshadowing of the doom it would bring. His fate, like his cup, was always bound to overflow.

Having fled to Phantasia Mountain, Eurytion has learned nothing from his past misfortunes. He continues to indulge his every whim without restraint. Many locals speak ill of him, but for now, there's not much they can do.

"Hahaha! More wine! More women!"

summary: A straightforward Guardian who specializes in stacking Magic Defense through [Runic Force] and entering the {wild} state as his HP drops. He sacrifices his own health to provide a substantial shield to allies with [Wildcry] at the start of battle. He deals solid cone-shaped physical damage with [Shock 'n' Awe] while buffing his team with {morale}.
lore: Dwarf warriors are the heart of the dwarven kingdom. With hammers in hand, they spend their days crafting blades and shaping steel. But when danger comes knocking, those same hands grip their hammers tight and stride fearlessly onto the battlefield.
Dwarf warriors are renowned for their unyielding resolve. When the need arises, they stand as living shields, forming a steadfast line of defense for their kin.

Beyond the battlefield, dwarven warriors are unmatched as master smiths. With every strike of the hammer, they forge not just weapons and armor, but a testament to their resolve—infusing steel with sweat, sorcery, and an unyielding hunger for battle and glory.

In daily life, dwarven warriors are all master drinkers—ale, rum, mead, even abyssal brew. They drink and sing in equal measure, and on days without war, such revelry is simply routine—loud, merry, and never in short supply.

The turmoil on Phantasia Mountain forced many dwarves to flee their ancestral home. Seizing the opportunity, wicked forces took possession of sacred dwarven vaults, passed down through generations. But the dwarves have not given up—they believe that one day, their kingdom will rise again.

summary: A frail but persistent Guardian who powers up as allies fall, gaining {deathrattle} stacks to increase his Attack via {shroud}. He bolsters physical defense by gaining {awakening} when allies use Overdrives, and deals magic area damage with [Stinkstorm] while protecting himself with a minor shield using [Hop 'n' Chop].
lore:
Mummification was once nothing more than a method for preserving the dead, but now (for reasons no one quite understands) some of the smaller mummies have begun to stir again, roaming far and wide across every realm...

"Life..."

Although slow and weak in combat, they still pose a serious threat when encountered in large numbers. They constantly mutter strange, unintelligible phrases, and it remains unclear whether they retain any sense of self-awareness.

Most of the time, they stagger like the walking dead—mindless, erratic, gnawing at anything that draws near. Yet at times, as if answering an unseen command, they shift—coordinated, purposeful, terrifying in their sudden unity.

"Decay..."

Perhaps because they lack what one would call true life, these beings are difficult to fully stop. Yet some among them are suddenly overwhelmed by fragments of memory from their past lives—driven into madness before crumbling into drifting sand.

"Born... again..."

In fact, their appearance is closely related to the necromancy of a certain pharaoh. Under the spell's summons, fragmented souls return from the underworld, inhabiting withered bodies and spilling into the world once more...

summary: A control-oriented Priest who marks enemies with Reaper's Gaze, allowing allies who attack them to recover HP and gain {blessing}. [Soul Hook Scythe] drags and stuns a distant target for focused fire, while [Void Prison] temporarily banishes Hela and an enemy from battle. [Soul Lamp] rescues critically injured allies with healing, repositioning, and a shield, giving her an unusual mix of disruption and emergency support.
title: Goddess of Death
lore:
Hela, the Queen of the Underworld, presides over death, disease, and aging. Due to a terrifying prophecy brought by her lineage, the King of the Gods, Odin, Banished her to the coldest and darkest realm of Helheim, commanding her to rule this land of the dead and to act as the supervisor for all souls who did not die in the glory of battle but passed away due to aging or sickness.

Named as a ruler, yet in truth a prisoner. During the long nights in Helheim, Hela gradually realized that she was trapped here because of the King of the Gods' helplessness in the face of prophecy. Just like these common souls, were they born only to end up in Helheim?

Confronted by the injustice of the Allfather and the cruelty of fate, Hela comes to believe that only she can uphold true justice. When the gods plead with her to restore Balder, the radiant god slain by Hodr, she sets forth a single condition: all things must weep for Balder. This is not an attempt to defy the law of death, but a deliberate trial. Why should the gods be granted the privilege of resurrection? The very notion reeks of inequity. Thus, when the giantess—Loki in disguise—refuses to shed a tear, Hela receives the outcome she intends. By withholding Balder's soul, she does not act out of spite, but in defense of an uncompromising law. It is a reminder to the gods themselves: before death, all beings stand equal.

In Helheim, under Hela's dominion, the souls of the noble Aesir and the lowliest creatures alike decayed at the same unhurried pace, swallowed by the same implacable silence. Yet in other reaches of the World Tree, life continued much as before. Hela came to see that her confinement to Helheim was itself a bitter irony—an affront to the equality she claimed to uphold.

A new thought took root in her mind: perhaps the prophecy spoke true. Before the final dissolution, all distinctions forged in life would be leveled, every value ground to nothing in the end.

Hela stepped willingly onto the stage of Ragnarok. At that moment, whether she had chosen the prophecy or the prophecy had shaped her no longer mattered.

As the fires of war spread across the realms, as Odin and his ancient foe Fenrir perished together, and as radiant Asgard collapsed into flame, Hela watched with unblinking calm. She saw the Valkyries of Valhalla fall one by one. The warriors once exalted in glory and the souls in her own realm who had died of sickness and age alike were reduced, in the cosmic conflagration, to the same indistinguishable ash. The prophecy came to pass in its most violent form, and the "ultimate equality" she had once questioned revealed itself at last—not as mercy, but as annihilation shared by all.

After Ragnarok, Hela arrived at Phantasia Mountain. Here, there is no distinction between Asgard and Helheim; sunlight can bathe every inch of land. To her, this is not exile, but a true release.

She knows that other survivors have also reached this promised land with her. Hela's gaze will be like writhing shadows, watching every figure attempting to rebuild order here. In this place, the essence of equality must be upheld until the end.
quote: Your soul will ultimately belong to my realm.
ssr_quote: Your soul will be my most prized collection!

title: Love Goddess
lore: Venus, goddess of love and beauty, is known as the "Grace of the Gods." Radiant and divine, her presence inspires affection, desire, and awe in equal measure.

She is merciful, she is the purifier of sin, the rider on horseback, the veiled one. Funnily enough, she is also the goddess of orchards... Symbols associated with her include doves, apples, bees, swans, guavas, and roses.

She was born from the foam of the sea.

"From the waves she came, mother of all things. She sows love, nurtures life—everything upon this earth is her harvest."
During the golden apple affair, Venus promised Paris the love of the most beautiful mortal woman—Helen. That vow became the spark that ignited the Trojan War.
Even in the face of love so deep it defies reason, Venus shows mercy—Galatea, after all, was granted life under just such a blessing.

summary: A Priest whose healing can critically strike, turning excess recovery into shields. [Soulbond Healing] bounces between allies, while [Stun Potion] ricochets between enemies to interrupt them. Her Overdrive, [Shallow Burial], sharply lowers an ally's current HP but grants death immunity, offensive buffs, and repeated healing that restores the health sacrificed by the cast.
title: Queen of Sheba
lore:
Queen of Sheba Bice, the monarch of the ancient Sheba kingdom, renowned for her immense wealth and extraordinary intellect. She once led a massive caravan laden with spices, gems, and gold across the desert to Jerusalem, where she tested the famous King Solomon of Israel with the Wisdom Quiz. From then on, she left behind multiple personas in the annals of various civilizations and oral traditions.


“She came to Jerusalem with a very great retinue, with camels bearing spices, a lot of gold, and gems. She came to Solomon and told him all that was on her mind.”
——1 Kings

Bice is naturally beautiful and exceptionally intelligent, yet she never flaunts these qualities. She harbors a passion for knowledge and wisdom that transcends borders. Upon hearing of Solomon's wisdom, she challenged the legendary wise king with countless difficult questions. When Solomon answered them effortlessly, she was not angered by her 'failure.' Instead, she openly acknowledged his superior wisdom and presented him with generous gifts. This pure reverence and pursuit of wisdom has been the foundation of her approach to life.

"I had heard reports about you and your wisdom in my country, and now I see they are true. I did not believe what was said until I came and saw it with my own eyes. Indeed, not even half was told to me."
—1 Kings

Aside from the world-shaking voyage, Bice spent her life in her kingdom fulfilling her duties as a builder and Ruler. Under her governance, the ancient Kingdom of Sheba, centered around its capital Marib, constructed a monumental and exquisitely crafted massive dam that sustained water supply for twelve centuries, nourishing an entire civilization. To her, ruling was not merely about accumulating wealth but about constructing immortal projects, using Intellect and resources to create a prosperous homeland for her people.

Beyond ruling over the masses and constructing great achievements, Bice harbored a little-known pastime—a refined interest in studying the properties of flora and the art of healing. The land of Sheba was abundant with spices, myrrh, and various exotic plants. During breaks from her duties, she would often wander alone in the Old Royal Palace gardens or the remote countryside, personally gathering herbs and experimenting with the preparation of potions with different effects. To her, understanding the nature of all things and easing her people's suffering were also essential pursuits of a ruler.
However, this hobby, born from compassion and a thirst for knowledge, earned her demonized misinterpretations. In some Legends far removed from Sheba, this queen—renowned for her Mastery of pharmacology—gradually became smeared with the shadow of being labeled a 'witch doctor' or even a 'demon queen.'

As the queen of a foreign land, Bice is renowned for her wisdom and wealth, yet burdened by misunderstandings due to differing Legends and Sacred Faiths.
Upon arriving at Phantasia Mountain, this queen—who once traveled across lands to seek wisdom and truth—finally found a place where everything could be discussed equally. Her current goal is to find souls capable of penetrating appearances and perceiving the essence, to explore the art of governance, the source of faith, and the answer to a millennia-old question that has plagued her: When future generations can no longer witness my wisdom and achievements firsthand, how should they define the truth of who I am?
quote: Let us listen to the voices of all souls!
ssr_quote: Do you want to turn into a frog?

summary: An elemental-synergy Priest who builds [Elemental Alchemy] stacks to permanently buff the team's critical and attack stats. She launches bouncing heals and applies {chill} during her channeled [Elemental Symphony]. She excels at disrupting enemy Overdrives by manipulating energy costs through [Elemental Crucible] while applying {heal_block}.
title: Starlight Witch
lore: Morgana, a witch with the blood of British royalty. As the illegitimate eldest daughter of King Uther and the half-sister of King Arthur, she was secretly sent to the royal library from a young age to study ancient astrology under the guidance of a mentor. The magic power flowing through her veins intertwined with the resonance of the stars, quickly making her the court's sole stargazer. From the stars, she glimpsed the remnants of civilization, and under their revelation, she learned ancient astrological magic, thus binding her fate closely with the starry sky.

Morgana walks the ruins and forgotten lands, gathering lost knowledge and relics fallen from the stars. In time, she comes to understand that within the shadows of history lie the hidden doctrines of the heavens, and within the turning of the celestial spheres resound the echoes of the mortal world. In the constellations, she foresees the Sword in the Stone breaking free from its prison of rock. She also perceives the arc of Camelot's inevitable fall. Though she strives to avert the tragedy, she finds herself powerless before the immutable will inscribed among the stars. When at last the dust settles, she stands undone—overwhelmed, and ultimately claimed by the very heavens she once sought to read.

Morgana devoted herself to deciphering the resonance between the stars and the mortal world. She believed the paths of the constellations were history inscribed upon the heavens, while the ruins scattered across the earth were star charts sunk into soil. She did more than preserve the records of civilization—she sought to unravel the hidden correspondences between sky and stone, searching for the ultimate equation that might reconcile star and dust as one. To her, only through understanding this resonance could one foresee the cadence of civilizations rising and falling, and perhaps even brush against the underlying laws that govern the turning of the world.

The guidance of the stars led Morgana to mistakenly believe that she was their sole child in the mortal realm. That illusion shattered during a pivotal interpretation. Within ancient ruins, she aligned a fragment of lost history with a precise celestial trajectory in flawless correspondence. In doing so, she uncovered a forbidden truth—and drew down the heavens' reprisal. In agony, she came to understand that to read too deeply into the stars is to invite the cold gaze that dwells beyond them. From that moment, her body began to wither at an unnatural pace. Yet in that ruin lay clarity as well: she was never the chosen of the stars, only another mortal who had stared too long into their light.

At that time, Morgana, who had come to Phantasia Mountain, had not gazed at the Starry Sky for a long time. Yet one chance glance revealed a sky unlike any she had known. After long inner turmoil, she chose once more to pursue the heavens. She will now continue her research and complete the magic of the stars—and this time, whatever the cost, she will not turn away.

title: Holyblade Bishop
lore: She is the Archbishop of the Church of Gram, bearing the solemn duty of guiding the faithful and upholding the sacred teachings of the order.

Legend has it that the hero who wields the holy sword will bring a dawn of hope to the world. Ophelia has devoted her life to Gram, the sacred blade, and waits in silence for the day that destined hero finally appears.

Before joining the Church of the Sacred Blade, Ophelia was a ballet dancer. Strange occurrences often followed her—unexplained events that eventually led her to seek refuge within the church. Only after becoming one of its own did she begin to understand—everything she had experienced was the call of the divine sword, Gram.

Ophelia's devotion was plain for all to see. Her faith and deeds moved countless others, drawing more and more followers to her side. With their support, she eventually rose to the position of Archbishop.
Every believer of the Church of the Sacred Blade firmly believes that under the guidance of Ophelia and the sacred sword, Gram, all evil on Phantasia Mountain will one day be purged.

summary: A probability-based Priest whose skills have a high chance to trigger multiple times via [Wish Fulfillment]. She provides massive team healing and powerful buffs like {morale} and {fervor} through [Wish Granted]. She generates {awakening} stacks when allies use Overdrives, which she consumes to guarantee her skill duplications and reduce team energy costs.
title: Wishing Genie
lore:
According to legend, the ancient king of Sasan left behind a magic lamp—one that, when awakened, would summon a genie to grant three wishes. When someone finally uncovered the lamp, the spirit they called forth introduced herself as Scheherazade—bright, cheerful, and eager to help. She's certainly enthusiastic... but perhaps not quite as all-powerful as the stories claimed...

"Tell me everything—your true heart's desire!"

It turns out this genie doesn't actually have the power to grant wishes—but she still tries her best to help. She's more than happy to fulfill requests like cleaning the house or fighting off enemies, but struggles with wishes like "I want to make a fortune" or "Please make her love me again!" As a result, some have joked that she's less of a genie, and more of a magical personal assistant...

"Um... as long as I can help, I guess that's good enough?"

Scheherazade was once human. In the days of the cruel Sasanian king Shahryar—who took a new bride each day and executed her the next morning—she offered herself in marriage to stop the bloodshed. Each night, she told the king a captivating tale, always leaving the climax hanging at dawn. Eager to hear what came next, the king delayed her execution. And so her stories stretched across one thousand and one nights...

When the final tale was told, the king—now in love with Scheherazade—asked for her hand in marriage. But she refused to wed a man so steeped in blood. Instead, she left the Sasanian kingdom behind, setting out to share her stories with the world. The One Thousand and One Nights became beloved by the people, passed down for generations. Over time, small changes crept into the tales... and under the influence of Phantasia Mountain's power, fiction slowly began to spill into reality.

A character from One Thousand and One Nights brought into the real world, the soul of Scheherazade—once bound to stories—awakened within the magic lamp. Naturally cheerful, she quickly embraced her new reality and began earnestly exploring how her newfound powers might help others. Of course... this has led to more than a few well-intentioned mishaps.

"From storyteller to part of the story—what a wild experience... I'd better make the most of it!"

She manipulates the battlefield by cloning the strongest allied summons with [Soulshatter Coffin]. She permanently increases her own Max HP and Attack Speed whenever allied summons are defeated through [Dark Nourishment].
title: Guardian Maiden
lore: Spimo has wandered the Shattered Lands for a century, with no memory of her past or her destination, existing as little more than a living shell. Until one day, the will of the Ring of Dominion awakened within her like a spark, fully restoring her consciousness and reminding her of her mission as its guide. She felt the ring's call—to lead the destined one to it. From that moment on, her path gained purpose.

Spimo seeks the true bearer of the Ring of Dominion. Any ruler in the world could be the one she guides. She leads them toward the ring and into trials of fate. Many believe themselves chosen, only to fall. Again and again, she witnesses ambition and conviction shatter before the final judgment. None have passed every decree of the ring.

As another challenger fell, doubt crept into Spimo's heart. Was her guidance incomplete? That night, the Ring of Dominion spoke again. The true destined master had appeared. She set out without hesitation, walking the only correct path.

She finally met the fated master. Guided by her hand, the future Ringsworn overcame every trial and stood before the Ring of Dominion, placing it upon their finger. In that moment, Spimo's soul was filled with burning devotion, and she swore eternal loyalty to both ring and bearer. She followed silently, ever at their side, waiting for the call. Those were the only years of true peace she ever knew—until the seal descended upon the Ring of Dominion and its bearer, and all fell into silence.

Spimo disguised herself as a mortal and settled in Midham, the city closest to the seal.
She sometimes heard tavern patrons speak of the Ring of Dominion and merely smiled like any other listener.
In time, she discovered the chance she had awaited—the red-haired princess of Midham desperately needed unparalleled power to save her kingdom.
Everything that followed unfolded smoothly. The seal was broken, the Ring of Dominion returned to the world with its bearer, and Spimo quietly followed them once more, setting out on a new journey.
quote: I follow the commands of the Ringsworn.
ssr_quote: O master of the ring... I have been waiting for you.

title: Fairy Queen
lore:
Living by the shores of Avalon, the gentle and maternal Fairy Queen is beloved for her boundless compassion toward her kin. Graceful in form and gifted with powerful magic, she rules with quiet wisdom. Though calm and composed by nature, she occasionally gives in to a mischievous whim—playfully teasing the occasional human who wanders too close.

"Don't be so downcast. You can talk to me about anything."

Though her true age may rival that of the great mage Merlin—and rumors suggest the two once shared a late-blooming romance—any discussion of this topic is strictly forbidden. Despite her royal status, she's remarkably skilled at cooking and housework, and is equally at home in the palace and the kitchen. She treats her subjects like her own children, and is always fussing over the minutiae of their daily lives.

"Wh-What do you mean I'm nagging...? I just know what's best for you..."

In stark contrast to her queenly demeanor, she has an intense fondness for romantic gossip and daydreams about sweeping love stories. Eager to help humans find true love, she often goes so far as to use magic—love dust, charm spells, and the like. Though her efforts have caused more than a few laughable mishaps, her name has become well-known among humans because of them.

Deep down, she hopes the human world might one day become as beautiful as Avalon. To that end, she devotes herself to aiding the leaders of humankind, believing they may yet guide their people toward lasting prosperity. When Lancelot was entrusted to her care, she raised him with great dedication, shaping him into a knight of rare excellence. Later, to help Arthur reclaim his throne, she gifted him the Sword of Kings—forged by the fairies themselves.

Bearer of the Ring of Law. Many years ago, a fragment of the Ring of Dominion's power was drawn to Avalon, where it crystallized in a sacred spring. At Merlin's suggestion, she took the ring into her care, awaiting the one destined to wield it. But the ring's power soon drew the attention of evil beings from another world—unleashing a crisis unlike anything the Fairy Kingdom had ever faced.

"We are a peaceful people—but that doesn't mean we'll suffer in silence. Children, the time to fight has come."

name: Vivienne
summary: A unique possession-based Priest who attaches to the highest-attack ally using [Gleam of Refuge], rendering herself untargetable. While possessed, she provides her host with massive shields, Attack boosts, and continuous healing via [Sacred Spring’s Blessing]. She also supports her host by dealing damage and applying {chill} with [Cold Surge Water Bomb].
title: Lady of the Lake
lore:
A water nymph who takes on human form. She dwells at the heart of Lake Avalon, her presence fleeting and near-impossible to trace. Few have ever glimpsed her dance or heard her song—yet all who do agree: no language, however ornate, could ever capture the boundless wonder of that moment.

"Emerald mists float upon the lake's still heart, and within them stands a maiden of unearthly beauty." — Secrets of the Camelot Court

In that lake, there is a stone island, more beautiful than any place in the human world. The fairy on the stone island awaits the prophesied destined king to whom she will give the powerful sword. But what is the price for obtaining this power? 

"Please take the small boat and row to the center of the lake to retrieve the sword and Excalibur's Scabbard. As for the gift I desire, I will naturally ask for it when the time comes." — 'The Death of King Arthur'

Vivienne could never quite grasp humanity’s obsession with power—yet she earnestly seeks to understand their emotions. The swaddled infant left by the lake gave her a chance to truly connect with the human world. That child, strong and fearless, grew under her care into the greatest Knight of the Lake: Lancelot of the Round Table.

Those who crave power are ultimately consumed by it. Vivienne has witnessed too much, and even the destined king cannot escape the fate of madness. Countless adventurers who have heard the legend seek the beautiful Lady of the Lake to obtain the magical sword. Initially, Vivienne was willing to offer these adventurers the so-called "trials," but gradually, she grew weary of it. 

"Whoever wields this sword must bear its weight."

The hero travels alongside the dragon, the Ring of Dominion reappears in the world, and gods from other realms emerge... The calm of Phantasia Mountain is suddenly disrupted, yet Vivienne finds herself unexpectedly passionate—she wants to witness the fate of those two, whether they will break the cycle of destiny or succumb to its design.
quote: Did you drop this sword into the water...?

title: Arcane Lord
lore:
An elven mage who has dedicated her life to the study and practice of arcane magic. In battle, her strength is undeniable, and few can match her understanding and manipulation of magical sources. Once the leader of a renowned circle of mages, she has since stepped down and now travels the world in search of the true essence of the arcane.

"The power of magic calls to me."

Abandoned by her parents as an infant and later taken in by a wizard, she was raised under her mentor's guidance and began studying magic from a young age. She quickly demonstrated a natural affinity for spellcasting, mastering a wide array of spells with ease and adapting them skillfully for combat. In a decisive battle against a demon legion, she earned great distinction—and, with the support of her mentor and peers, rose to become the leader of the mage's order.

She despises those who abuse arcane power—especially villains who use it for unjust ends—and has led the mage order many times to root out corruption and evil. Known for her strict discipline, she holds her mages to high standards and leads by example, enforcing those same rules on herself. When not training or managing official duties, she has little time for personal affairs.

"We are noble warriors who carry the light of arcana—never forget the honor we uphold!"

During her training, she once reached a state of complete selflessness—her soul seemingly merging with the very source of arcane power. To her, this is the true pinnacle of a mage's path. Since then, she has gained the ability to sever her enemies' magical flow at its origin, unraveling their spells and emerging ever more unstoppable.

The more she studied arcane magic, the more she came to sense its depth, mystery, and brilliance. Driven by a desire to grow even stronger, she departed after the group had settled, bidding farewell to her companions. Now she travels the world in search of places where magic gathers and shifts—determined to reach the highest realm of understanding.

"Even I... have yet to grasp the true depths of the arcane."

title: Irongut Tyrant
lore: A shaman of the ogre tribe—lazy and gluttonous, like most of his kin—but with a twist of magical cunning. While he shares the intelligence common to spellcasters, in his case, it tends to manifest as trickery rather than wisdom.

What is Caligula's favorite food? That's right—it's boar! One look at him and it's obvious. After all, we're talking about a brute (well, a demon brute) who wears an entire boar as a scarf like it's nothing.

As a shaman of the ogre tribes, Caligula practices a form of magic unlike anything used by humans or elves. Human and elven mages tend to look down on ogre shamans, dismissing their spells as little more than cheap tricks.

Though a mage by title, Caligula rarely casts spells himself—he prefers sending his underlings to do the fighting. For those who disobey his orders, his usual punishment isn't magical at all: he simply smacks them on the head with his staff.

After hearing from the Wild Hunt that otherworldly gods were preparing to invade Phantasia Mountain, Caligula sensed an opportunity. Hoping to benefit from the coming chaos, he and his gang promptly pledged allegiance to Hades. Unfortunately for him, no matter whose banner he fights under, he always ends up getting thoroughly thrashed by the Ringsworn, much to his frustration.

title: Hero Mentor
lore:
Unlike most centaurs, Chiron is neither savage nor warlike. Said to be born of divine lineage, she carries a noble and formidable bloodline. A true polymath, she excels in music, strategy, literature, archery, swordplay—you name it. It's said that mastering even a single discipline under her guidance is enough to make one a force to be reckoned with.

"Different subjects come with different class hours—and, naturally, different tuition fees. So, student... which skill do you wish to learn?"

According to legend, Chiron lives in a cave on Pelion, where she trains only the most exceptional warriors. But her dwelling is no ordinary place, and few can find it. Those who wish to study under this legendary mentor must first cross forests and fog, scale mountains and ford streams, enduring countless trials just to stand before her. 

"Hmm... not bad. You've passed the first trial."

Though Chiron is honored as a wise mentor and sage, she bears a sorrow of her own. Her parents never truly accepted her—her mother, unable to endure the shame of birthing a centaur, chose to become a linden tree. Even now, Chiron quietly longs for the love and trust she was denied. It is a yearning she has never dared voice to another soul.

Chiron is well-read, well-spoken, and respected by many as a wise and gracious mentor. But oddly enough, her own kind—the centaurs—have never truly accepted her. In a dispute with a band of centaur raiders, she was struck by an arrow. The pain dragged on for months, growing so severe that even death began to seem like a mercy. It took her a long time to recover, and even now, the wound never fully left her.

After recovering from a grave illness, Chiron held no hatred toward her fellow centaurs, nor did she seek retribution. Instead, the ordeal awakened in her a deeper understanding of the power of knowledge and the purpose of teaching. She came to accept that her life would one day come to an end—but the path of wisdom could endure, carried forward by those who follow.

"What I know, what I’ve learned. Let it live on through others."
ssr_quote: Knowledge burns bright, passed down through generations

title: Spring Flower Spirit
lore:
A lively little sprite that often seen frolicking among the flowers and grass. She loves the bloom of spring and can understand the language of plants. Having spent her life in the elven flower fields, she remains cheerful, carefree, and open-hearted—even to strangers.

"I heard the flower buds whisper! They said spring is almost here!"

Born from the heart of a morning glory bloom, she sips dew for water and dines on flower nectar. As the youngest among the fairies, she's doted on by all. She spends her days caring for sick plants and has even cultivated a few flower breeds of her own in the garden. Sometimes, she sneaks off to play with the ancient Spirit Tree, who—according to her—has seen the whole history of the world and loves to share the best stories.

Flora gathered dew from the Spirit Tree and shared it with her kin, helping their people grow stronger through its power. The elders' praise made her proud. But the peace didn't last—monsters drawn by the dew's magic began to appear near the elves' flower fields. Naive and trusting, Flora didn't sense their ill intent. Instead, she warmly told them exactly where to find the Spirit Tree...

When Beowulf of the Wild Hunt struck down the Spirit Tree, Flora—who could hear its cries—was overwhelmed with panic. But the elves stood no chance against the Wild Hunt. Realizing the calamity she had helped cause, Flora was filled with regret. Ignoring the adults' warnings, she slipped away from the flower fields, hoping to aid the Spirit Tree—only to be captured by goblins along the way.

"I'm sorry... It's all my fault you're in so much pain...!"

Thanks to the help of the Ringsworn Legion, the Spirit Tree has regained its vitality. Flora realizes that there is still much evil in the world that she cannot comprehend. Determined to help more ailing and injured plants, she now sets out to strengthen herself and uncover the shadows that threaten the natural world.

"I want to grow stronger too, so the flowers will never have to cry again!"
quote: May hope and flowers bloom together~

title: Wandering Songstress
lore:
Cheerful and lively, she loves singing and playing with humans. However, any human who hears her singing goes mad and dies... Unfortunately, she doesn't seem to have realized this. Drifting from sea to sea, she's unwittingly inspired terrifying siren legends in every corner of the world.

"I just want my singing to reach every corner of the world!"

Loves the ocean just as much as she loves singing. When she's not "playing" with humans, she enjoys diving into the deep—admiring coral reefs, collecting shells, and treasure-hunting in shipwrecks. Naturally outgoing, she can befriend almost any sea creature... but don't mistake her for just another ordinary mermaid. She really hates that.

She sees the world differently from humans. Death isn't something to fear, in her eyes—it's simply the way mortals express their admiration for her voice. When hunger strikes, she doesn't shy away from eating human flesh. Ordinary people who hear a siren's song for more than thirty seconds tend to lose their minds. There's still a chance of recovery—if they escape the sound's reach in time. But doing so is likely to offend her.

"How cruel... you don't want to hear me sing?"

There was once a singer, devoted to the pursuit of art, who became obsessed with tales of the siren and set out to find her—willing even to die for a duet. Though she couldn't understand his fixation, the siren agreed to sing. After thirty seconds of perfect harmony, the man ended his life with a smile... and for the first time, the siren felt a trace of sorrow.

"So this is the beauty of harmony... If only this song could go on forever."

Perhaps in search of new duet partners, the siren left the sea and came to land. But life here isn't easy—she can't swim freely, her favorite seaweed is nowhere to be found, and terrified humans keep interrupting her singing. Even so, she complains while trying to connect with them. Deep down, she feels that all of this must be meaningful somehow.
ssr_quote: Please listen carefully to my song.

summary: A utility Priest that replaces basic attacks with [Drum Beat] to continuously grant {attack_speed_up} to the strongest ally. He unleashes [Tempo Tantrum] to provide full-team {excitement}, and offers targeted healing through [Drums of Sanctuary], which becomes significantly more potent for allies in the {wild} state.
lore:
Unlike a certain pair of less-than-brilliant brothers, this goblin has ambition. Big ambition. Armed with a dream (and a lot of noise), he's made it his mission to spread the spirit of rock 'n' roll across all of Phantasia Mountain. Whether anyone asked for it or not.

"Rock 'n' roll forever!"

Drawn to rock music out of a natural curiosity for all things new, he quickly became hooked and never looked back. Just as passionate about fashion, he carefully designs everything from his outfit to the patterns on his drumhead. Unfortunately, his bold sense of style often attracts the odd spot of teasing...

"Fools! What do you know? This is true fashion!"

Surrounded by tone-deaf fools, she left home in search of a place where true music could be born. On her journey, she crossed paths with a siren who loved to sing. At first, it seemed like destiny—until they realized their musical tastes clashed harder than cymbals in a thunderstorm. The bickering turned to battle, and... well, the future rock legend got absolutely wrecked.

"A goblin? In a rock band?" "Pfft—what a joke! Even dumber than those two brothers... hah!" That's the kind of sneering he came home to. Most goblins might've given up—but not one powered by pure rock 'n' roll. The more they laughed, the louder he played.

"Real rock is the guts to rage against the grain!"

Of course, the pursuit of music is more important than the Ring of Dominion! Although he says that, it's hard not to be tempted by the ring's power. And so, he has begun fighting mid-performance—determined to spread the spirit of rock, even to his enemies!

title: Guide Fairy
lore:
A cheerful, fluttering sprite and loyal companion to Princess Siegfried, Viel serves as the ever-reliable helper of the Ringsworn Legion. Though not much of a fighter, her powerful healing magic and natural elven senses often prove unexpectedly useful in the thick of adventure.

"I'm just so happy I get to help Her Highness and Lord Ringsworn!"

Simple and kind-hearted, she spends her days blowing dandelions, collecting glowing pebbles, and watching Siegfried swinging at target dummies. Despite her simple interests, she's surprisingly well-versed in runic knowledge and is able to decipher many ancient, obscure texts. Though she has an excellent sense of direction, she claimed to be lost in the forest the day Siegfried rescued her. Since then, she has made no effort to return to her people.

Every time Siegfried was wounded in training, it was Viel who healed him. Though the pain was sharp, the young princess's eyes never lost their sparkle. She would chatter endlessly about her favorite tales of heroes, the light in her voice warming Viel's heart more deeply than any spell ever could.

"The princess's dreams are my dream, and every injury she suffers... I'll be the one to mend it!"

On the day the wyrm Ladon attacked, Viel did everything in her power to protect Siegfried. But she knew—some wounds can never be healed. All she could do was stand beside her and keep watch. Even when Siegfried spoke of freeing Fafnir, a dream few believed in, Viel stood firmly by her side.

"Princess... you're crying. Please, don't waste your tears on a fate we can't change..."

Though her days with the Ringsworn Legion are filled with chaos, Viel sometimes grows quiet, lost in thought. Being caught in a crisis that threatens the world may be too heavy a burden for a tiny sprite like her... but her resolve remains strong, guiding the party toward the unknown.

title: Queen of the Underworld
lore:
Hades, Queen of the Underworld, is the embodiment of death and the realm beyond. Often called the "Zeus of the Afterlife," she presides over death, souls, and the great beyond. Her divine task is to maintain balance, ensuring that each departed soul is judged fairly and granted its rightful place. 

"No soul shall escape."

Hades resides year-round in the shadowy depths of the underworld, which connects to Tartarus—the prison where the defeated Titans were cast after the Titanomachy. Within the underworld flow four great rivers, marking the realm where souls of the dead gather, and where the cycle of death and rebirth begins.

Long ago, when the three gods—Hades, Poseidon, and Zeus—cast lots to divide the world, it was Hades who drew the Underworld, and thus he became its sovereign. Perhaps it was in that moment that the first seed of rebellion quietly took root in his heart.

The Underworld is where the defeated Titans are imprisoned—even Zeus's own father, Cronus, is locked away there. The Goddess of Vengeance resides there as well, punishing mortals and gods who have committed eternal crimes. As ruler of this realm, how long can she cling to her ancient oath in this hellish domain without breaking it?

No one knows exactly how Hades learned of the Ring of Dominion—but legends speak of its divine power, capable of granting its bearer any wish. After centuries of gathering strength in the shadows, she sees her moment at last. The time has come to reshape the order... and rewrite the rules.

"Rules are made to be broken."
ssr_quote: Be submerged in the River Styx.
