name: Hermes
summary: An Ignite-focused Assassin who controls the battlefield through fire zones and forced movement. [Flame Stone Formation] reduces enemy healing and Critical Resistance, while [Lava Spikes] launches targets and applies {ignite}. Repeated Ignite and displacement effects build Energy and Overheat stacks, eventually sending Hermes into a fast-moving board-riding state that repeatedly damages and knocks back nearby enemies.
title: God of Swiftness
lore: Hermes is one of the twelve Olympian gods of Mount Olympus, known for his cleverness and cunning. He is the ancient Greek god in charge of trade, herding, theft, and travel, and also serves as the herald and messenger of the gods. As the guide of the divine, human, and underworld realms, he symbolizes the crossing of boundaries and becomes a key presence connecting different dimensions. "Farewell, Hermes, the Benefactor, the Guide, the Blesser!" — 'Homeric Hymns'

Hermes, naturally mischievous and curious, began her association with theft in her Juvenile Phase: she stole fifty of Apollo's cattle under the cover of night, walking backward to confuse her tracks. This cunning deeply tied her to the image of a thief. Apollo, enraged, confronted her, but she skillfully responded and offered a lyre made from a tortoise shell, turning his anger into joy. It is precisely because of her extraordinary eloquence and sharp mind that she can navigate effortlessly among the gods' entanglements and become the Exclusive witness and forger of Covenants, which is why she became the goddess of commerce.

As the guide of the dead, Hermes often crosses The River Styx with her golden staff in the twilight, illuminating the path for lost souls. She adheres to the neutrality of a guide, witnessing the Finale of heroes and mortals, yet never interferes with the rules out of personal feelings. "At that time, the night covered the earth; in the darkness, the messenger saw Hermes approaching from not far ahead." — "The Iliad"

Hermes possesses the divine speed to traverse great distances in an instant and the insight to see through illusions. When Zeus needs to gather information from various realms, he always dispatches Hermes to weave through the clouds. She conveyed the will of the gods during the Trojan War and secretly delivered crucial weapons to heroes in distress. "Hermes, since you handle other matters, you are also my messenger; now, I want you to teleport this decree without setback; let the strong-willed Odysseus begin his odyssey and return to his homeland." — 'The Odyssey'

After arriving at Phantasia Mountain, Hermes's protection for the traveling wayfarers has never waned. She continues to walk tirelessly, traversing every edge of this realm, ensuring that every path remains open, and every voice finds its echo. With her divine trait of crossing boundaries, she allows the isolated worlds within this phantasmic realm to hear each other's echoes.

lore: A cold-eyed, quiet girl who always travels alone. She rarely speaks, and no one knows where she came from or what she's searching for.
A long, long time ago, the fire god Loki and the giantess Angrboda spawned three evil offspring, one of whom was Jormungandr.
Jormy has lived alone for as long as she can remember and knows very little about the rules or customs of human society.
Even Jormy herself doesn't fully understand the ancient bloodline she carries. But now, a group known as the Wild Hunt has set its sights on the power within her.
Though her time with the Ringsworn and the others was short, it left a lasting impression on Jormy's heart. Parting was her idea—after all, how else could they have a tearful reunion someday?

title: Queen of Eternal Night
lore:
Lilith, the night demoness of Mesopotamia, the first female born in Hebrew Mythology, and the queen who rules the night.
Since her genesis in Eden, she has fought against the higher powers, angrily uttering the unspeakable true name, and thereby gaining the strength to fly away from God's sacred garden. When three angels found her again, she refused to return and instead turned to the ever-churning red sea.

"He has set fire and water before you; reach out your hand and choose what you desire.
Life and death are set before each person; what one chooses, one shall receive."—The Book of Sirach

Lilith's rebellion succeeded, but it came at a cost: her existence and records were erased by the gods and their creations. She roams the edges of the world, forever accompanied by darkness and curses, with her name mentioned only in the Dead Sea Scrolls or other heretical texts.

"The wild beasts of the desert shall also meet with the jackals... and Lilith shall rest there, finding a place of rest for herself."—Isaiah

Daylight belongs to the dominion of the gods; Lilith's kingdom unfurls only after the sun sinks beyond the horizon. She gathers the darkness and its curses, drawing them into herself and weaving them into her own power. If the world requires a vessel to contain all shadow and desire, then she will willingly take up that sinful crown.

"Her disgrace shall never be blotted out; her name shall become a curse."—The Book of Sirach

And so, in the land of Nod, east of Eden, she finds Cain—fellow exile, first murderer. The curse passes between them, deepening and taking root. From that day forth, the first of the bloodbound is born.
"Flee from sin as from a serpent.
If you draw near to it, it will devour you."—The Book of Sirach

As night falls, Lilith's figure appears alongside it in Phantasia Mountain. She spreads her wings, eagerly embracing this unfamiliar yet brand-new territory. She will control the night here, strengthening her power... until she successfully ascends, and all vampires are treated equally with the creations of other deities.
quote: I fight against the powers that be, free in the darkness.

Serve the king under a hidden identity, but only for now. One day, you can overthrow him and take his place!
False loyalty deceived Arthur and even personally draped the Round Table Knight's cloak over her.

Will the king of the future remember her, and if so, how? As an old friend once lost? A traitor who defied the crown?
Or perhaps... as a blood relative, bound by fate, yet never truly known?

name: Pan Junbao
summary: A disruptive, Taunt-heavy Assassin who continuously forces enemies to attack him using [Showstopper Smash] and his [Serenity] talent. He mitigates incoming ranged basic attacks by intercepting them with [Featherweight Force] to charge up heavy physical damage, and transitions into a rapid-striking, lifesteal-heavy fighter when he enters the {wild} state.
title: Taichi Master
lore: A kung fu master who roams freely across mountains and rivers, living by the principle of unity between knowledge and action. Sightings of him on Phantasia Mountain are rare and fleeting—whether deep in perilous magic realms or passing quietly through bustling city squares, the black-and-white figure of this eastern panda is hard to miss... and even harder to follow. Before long, he vanishes without a trace, like a falling leaf on the wind.

Before mastering the art of Tai Chi, Pan Junbao was just an ordinary restaurant cook. With his round belly and short limbs, few believed he had any talent for martial arts—especially in a town where everyone knew how to fight. To many, he was little more than a walking punchline.

"They don't get it—being great at kung fu doesn't hold a candle to being great at cooking."

Kung Pao chicken, spicy boiled pork, shredded pork in garlic sauce, twice-cooked pork, mapo tofu, spicy shrimp, eggplant with minced meat, dry-fried green beans—when it comes to cooking, few can rival Pan Junbao. But skill alone doesn't satisfy him. He's tasted many foreign dishes, each with flavors unlike anything he's made himself. With pack on back and chopsticks in hand, he's set out into the world, swearing to sample every dish under the sun.

Having big dreams is all well and good—until reality hits you like a frying pan to the face. For the overly idealistic Pan Junbao, it wasn't wild beasts that got him at first, but simply getting lost. He wandered the deep forest for nearly two weeks, ran into a legendary monster, and then promptly fell off a cliff. Not the most graceful beginning...

Luckily, fortune was smiling on Pan Junbao. Even after falling from a cliff, he was rescued by a reclusive kung fu master. To escape the treacherous wilderness, Junbao became the master's disciple and began training in a powerful martial art known as "Tai Chi."

"Turns out kung fu and cooking aren't so different... it's all about controlling that energy flow."
quote: Manifest the universe, unite with the qi.

name: Rin
summary: An evasion-focused Assassin whose dodge rate scales massively with {deathrattle} stacks and innately through [Niten Ichiryu]. She summons a highly evasive {sword_clone} that taunts enemies, which she can later absorb to recover health and gain {dodge_up} using [Phantom Martial Soul], and deals untargetable, massive area damage with her [Swallow Return] Overdrive.
title: Peerless Swordmaster
lore: Rin was born into a family renowned for their swordsmanship, famous for the "Two-Sword Style" technique. Throughout a lifetime of over sixty battles, Rin remained undefeated, even achieving victories against formidable foes using only a wooden sword. Rin became known worldwide as a master duelist, leaving behind numerous legendary tales.

In the minds of many, Rin ought to be a stern, unsmiling samurai. In truth, she is a forthright and spirited swordswoman. Through years of relentless training, she comes to grasp the true essence of the blade—strength is not measured by the number of foes one defeats, but by what one chooses to protect. With this awakening, she evolves from a warrior who chases victory for its own sake into a guardian who draws her sword for others. Her blade gains warmth, and the road before her widens in turn.

Throughout Rin's life runs a single, unwavering pursuit: the state of "emptiness." In her early years, she is a swordswoman driven by victory. In time, she awakens to the deeper truth of non-killing, and at last arrives at a tranquil clarity in which all things are understood as void. She continually surpasses herself, breaking free from the confines of technique. What begins as swordsmanship is refined into art; what was once slaughter becomes dialogue. Through this pursuit, her blade gains a rare duality—it can cleave the hardest steel, yet also sever the most intangible threads of fate.

Rin never hesitates to teach her swordsmanship, yet she has never found the one true prodigy to inherit it. Her forthright, openhearted nature draws friends easily, but along the path of the blade, she walks alone. At last, she leaves her familiar dojo behind and sets out once more on the road of discipline. This time, she seeks not merely a student, but a companion in the Way—a successor, a catalyst for change, a new evolution of the sword itself.

By a twist of fate, Rin arrived at Phantasia Mountain, seeing it as a new starting point for her training. In this place where strong individuals from various realms gather, she wields her bamboo sword, making friends through combat, and refines her swordsmanship with each encounter. She hopes to explore the infinite possibilities of swordsmanship through exchanges with swordsmen from different worlds and continue on this endless path.
quote: The body may die, but the name of a samurai can never be abandoned!
ssr_quote: Oh? Do you wish to spar with me?

name: White Tiger
summary: A relentless Assassin who sacrifices her own health to unleash a devastating flurry of strikes with [Soaring Tempest], gaining massive Life Steal in the process. She permanently ignores enemy Physical Defense through [Soulshaker] and becomes unstoppable in the {wild} state, gaining immunity to stat reductions and transforming her basic attacks into [Infinity Combo] attacks.
title: Four Saints
lore:
A beast-tailed girl from a distant, mysterious kingdom in the East. Cheerful, energetic, and fond of food and fighting, she seems harmless enough—at first glance. In truth, she is the White Tiger, guardian deity of the West, whose power shakes the seas and whose magic knows no bounds. For reasons unknown, she now wanders the world in a youthful guise.

"Hmph! Mess with the tiger, and you'll get the claws!"

The White Tiger is one of the Four Divine Beasts, along with the Azure Dragon, Vermilion Bird, and Black Tortoise. Once celestial constellations, they absorbed the essence of heaven, the sun, the moon, and Earth to become gods, watching over the humans who revere them. The White Tiger often appears in autumn and is the god of battle and bloodshed—brave, commanding, and long regarded as the guardian of warriors and a symbol of protection against evil.

She grants the blessing of victory to those who fight bravely and serve their nation with unwavering loyalty. Throughout history, many undefeated generals have been hailed as reincarnations of the White Tiger Star, and she is honored by the people as the Divine Marshal of War. In times of chaos and upheaval, she is said to appear quietly among mortals—summoning wind and rain, turning the tide of battle, and guiding the course of history from the shadows.

She uses her magic to ward off disasters and uphold justice, often descending in human form to vanquish monsters and demons. Once the job is done, she vanishes without fanfare—her only request being a hearty meal as thanks. Though tales of her bravery are told far and wide, few would ever guess that the cheerful, super-strong girl is in fact a divine beast from the heavens.

"By the command of the sacred wards—begone, foul spirits and fiends!"

She appeared in the mortal realm this time after sensing the signs of an approaching disaster and the distortion of time and space. However, this world's delicious food and curious novelties have also captured her interest more than she expected...

"A storm is brewing... the world is on the verge of chaos."

name: Zagreus
summary: A highly mobile Assassin who blinks into combat and unleashes blizzards with [Storm Snowpiercer] while frequently applying {chill} and {freeze}. She severely restricts enemy Rage regeneration and deals massive bonus damage to frozen or elementally-debuffed targets, excelling at rapidly executing single targets while untargetable with [Swiftshadow Execution].
title: Nether Princess
lore: Zagreus is the daughter of Hades, ruler of the Underworld. At her birth, Hades received a prophecy foretelling that the Underworld princess would face a destined death and be reborn as a god. Unwilling to let his daughter suffer such pain, Hades guarded her strictly and even forbade her from leaving the Underworld.

Years of overprotection had already driven a wedge between mother and daughter, and their opposing ideals only deepened the divide. Zagreus refused to aid her mother, yet could not betray the Underworld. Her only choice was to flee.

After choosing to flee, the princess secretly explored the edges of the Underworld. Each escape ended in capture, but each failure strengthened her resolve. Through countless attempts, Zagreus grew stronger. During one escape, she met Athena. With Athena's help, she finally reached the mortal world.

Living among mortals, Zagreus witnessed the natural cycle of birth, aging, illness, and death, and saw how the law of death sustained order in the world. This led her to reflect on the responsibility she bore as the daughter of the Underworld. Perhaps her duty was never merely to escape.

"I won't run anymore. I have to stop this disaster."

Upon learning that Hades had gathered the armies of the Underworld to attack Phantasia Mountain, Zagreus set out at once. Disguised as Perseus, she aided the Ringsworn along the way, yet deep down she still hoped her mother would turn back.

"You cannot continue down this path. Olympus cannot endure another war."
quote: Give thanks for this princess's royal favor!
ssr_quote: Dare to deceive me? I'll send you to Tartarus.

She executes low-health targets with [Hunting Time], resetting the skill's cooldown upon a successful kill, and empowers her basic attacks with [Predatory Pulse] to inflict {shock} before unleashing a rapid barrage of strikes with [Furious Flurry].
title: Night Huntress
lore:
A stealthy, human-like beast that slips through the night without a sound. With swift, razor-sharp claws, it delivers a deadly strike before vanishing without a trace. It lives entirely in the wild—active by night, resting by day—free-spirited and driven by an untamed passion for the hunt.

"Once I've set my sights on my prey, there's no escape, meow!"

Hates being mistaken for a cat. Although she looks like one and often meows when she speaks, her true form is that of a fierce direwolf with fangs sharp enough to bite through any enemy. Coupled with her self-proclaimed moniker "Fenrir," everything suggests that this mysterious being is far from as simple as she appears...

In ancient legend, there was a monstrous wolf born in the age of the gods—brother to Jormungandr, the World Serpent, and Hel, goddess of death. It bit off the hand of Tyr, god of war, and was bound by the gods in magical chains. But when Ragnarok came, it broke free, unleashing its vengeance upon the gods and devouring Odin himself... and its name was Fenrir.

Though she bears the same name, her connection to the legendary tales remains unclear. It's said that two great powers once split from the giant wolf Fenrir—one to devour the sun, the other to hunt the moon. Perhaps her strength is tied to them. Some even suspect that "Fenrir" isn't her real name at all...

"Still so curious about me? Naughty, naughty! Mystery is a girl's best friend, meow!"

Though shrouded in mystery, she doesn't seem nearly as wicked as the legends claim. Her pursuit of the Ring of Dominion appears more about having fun than unleashing destruction. That said, her free-spirited ways can cause problems for others from time to time—like bathing wherever she pleases...

"Once I've got the Ring of Dominion, all the little fish in this river will be mine, meow... Hehe..."
quote: I can't lend you my claws, meow~

summary: A highly mobile Assassin whose Damage Amplification increases based on the total distance she has moved during the battle via [Long March]. She charges through enemies to deal physical damage and stun them with [Solar Steed], synergizing heavily with [Elemental Reactions] to continuously reduce her cooldowns and instantly dispel debuffs in the {grace} state.
title: Knight of the Lake
lore:
A knight raised by the Fairy of the Lake, known for her passionate spirit, cheerful nature, and unwavering dedication to justice. With a pure heart and noble ideals, she is often called the "Knight of the Lake." Her every action exemplifies the virtues of chivalry. As King Arthur's close companion and the most renowned of the Knights of the Round Table, she has long fought tirelessly to protect Camelot. 

"To realize a knight's glory, humility and bravery are virtues we must uphold."

After hearing of King Arthur's great reputation, she traveled from afar to Camelot, willing to serve this wise monarch. Upholding the spirit of a Knight, she earned King Arthur's trust, and their relationship grew close.

But under the treachery of Morgan le Fay, Lancelot came to believe that Arthur had betrayed him—and he became cold and distant. Arthur, wounded by the mistrust, faced their first bitter quarrel. In the end, she banished Lancelot from Camelot, and found herself more alone than ever before.

Yet her heart never strayed from Camelot. When she learned of the Wild Hunt's invasion, she rushed back—only to find she was too late. After the crisis was resolved by the Ringsworn Legion, she sat in deep conversation with King Arthur, and many long-standing grievances were finally put to rest. Lancelot chose to return, to help rebuild Camelot from its ruins. 

"My king... what you truly needed to protect was beside you all along."

After Arthur's departure, she inherited her will, guarding the peace of Camelot in her stead, and holding her memory close to heart. None were allowed to speak ill of the great king she once followed. Though the glory of the Round Table could never be revived, and the radiance of the Holy Grail was lost to time, she vowed to serve the people of Camelot with all that remained of her strength, for as long as life remained in her.

"None may judge your rights or wrongs. To me and to Camelot—you are, and shall ever be the one true king."
quote: In the name of the sun!

name: Nemesis
summary: A rapid-striking Assassin who blinks behind targets to deal massive physical damage and inflict {silence} with [Silent Scream]. She specifically targets and suppresses high-energy enemies using [Crippling Strike], throwing poison darts at targets with the highest Overdrive Energy costs while gaining massive Attack Speed boosts after casting Overdrives through [Endless Battle].
title: Goddess of Vengeance
lore:
The goddess of vengeance from Olympus, she delivers harsh and unflinching judgment upon all who break the law. Cold and merciless, she shows no hesitation in punishing the guilty. To wounded or weary warriors, she offers hatred as fuel for their fighting spirit. A symbol of judgment and retribution, she brings righteous deliverance to those who suffer injustice.

"Those steeped in sin—pay the price with your life!"

In a remote and shadowed corner of Tartarus, Nemesis built a prison of her own design. She spends most of her time patrolling its depths, rarely interacting with the other gods of Olympus. Within its walls are imprisoned the most wicked souls from every age—each condemned to eternal punishment, forever barred from reincarnation. Should any soul escape, Nemesis will pursue them to the ends of the earth.

She hunts down perjurers, those who persecute outsiders, and those who murder their own kin—no matter how far or how long they run, she shows no mercy. Once, a man who had killed his wife in a moment of rage wept and begged her for understanding, accusing the goddess of being unyielding. But Nemesis did not waver. She punished him coldly, without a word.

"Sin will not escape. Hatred will not fade. My purpose is not for mortals to question."

She shows no mercy to wrongdoers, yet holds deep sympathy for those who suffer without cause. She has heard the helpless cries of mothers robbed of their children, and the desperate pleas of refugees displaced by war. To her, vengeance is the fuel that keeps the wounded moving forward—and the means by which she offers them salvation.

"I swear—those who deserve punishment will taste the very pain you suffer today."

Many who found vengeance with Nemesis's aid chose to follow her, and over time, she quietly built a well-trained mortal army. Hades, lord of the underworld, grew increasingly displeased with her unauthorized interference in matters of the soul, and seeing the strength of the force she had gathered, he began seeking ways to turn it to his own ends. Now, longing to overthrow the order of Olympus, Hades has begun tempting her—to join him as his loyal servant.

title: Shadow Ronin
lore: Arriving like a shadow, vanishing like the wind—none may threaten the royal family of Midham while the Shadow Dancer stands watch. Bound by a single creed—to protect, without fail—the Shadow Dancer bears no name, only a codename spoken in whispers.

These aren't your average bodyguards. Shadow Dancers slink through shadows, sworn to a single lord. Whether it's tailing a target or slipping a blade between ribs—they get the job done unseen.

"Where there's light, there must be shadow."

Most Shadow Dancers are orphans. Before their training begins, the organization conducts a thorough investigation into each child's background to ensure there are no risks. Only then does training commence—harsh, unforgiving, and designed to eliminate the weak. Out of every ten recruits, only one typically survives to become a true Shadow Dancer.

When Ladon attacked, Prince Siegmund ordered Bladeheart to secretly protect Siegfried from the shadows. At first, she refused—after all their years together, she had long since resolved to give her life for Prince Siegmund, not anyone else. But deep down, she understood why he had given that command.

"Protect Siegfried. Bladeheart... this is my final order."

"I am the blade of the princess!" The moment she saw the evil dragon, this thought arose in her mind. And as for that so-called ringbearer? He's reckless. Dangerous. Untrustworthy. Rather than focusing solely on the enemy, Bladeheart keeps a close eye on him instead. A stranger with no clear past or origin... could he really be the one from the prophecy? The one meant to stand beside Princess Siegfried atop Phantasia Mountain and sever fate itself?
ssr_quote: The time has come, it must be done.

title: Twilight Beast
lore: A ferocious and savage werewolf, with blood-red eyes that betray an unending thirst for violence. Whether he retains any self-awareness, or is simply a beast driven by pure instinct, remains a matter of fear-fueled speculation.
Sure, his name might match a certain female feline—but this fluffy fellow's got fangs. Still not convinced? Pop your hand in his mouth. If you make it out unscathed, maybe he is a cat after all.

Long, long ago, the fire god Loki and the giantess Angrboda had three children—the eldest of whom was the monstrous wolf Fenrir. When Ragnarok came, Fenrir broke free of the chains the gods had placed upon him and devoured Odin himself—only to be torn in half by Odin's son, Vidar.
It is said that from then on, there were two Fenrirs in the world—one chasing the sun, the other the moon. Whether this werewolf is truly one of them remains uncertain.

On bright nights when the moon is full, Fenrir unleashes a terrifying howl. If he truly is the savage beast who once devoured Odin himself, then perhaps his cries beneath the moon are more than instinct—perhaps they echo a hunger to devour the moon itself.

name: Boar Knight
summary: A straightforward charging Assassin who drastically increases his Attack Speed and empowers his third strike using the [Focus] talent. He relies on his [Wild Charge] to plow through enemy lines, dealing physical damage to both his primary target and anyone in his path, and utilizes [Space Cadet] to deal area physical damage while reducing energy costs.
lore:
Unlike a certain pair of foolish brothers, this goblin fancies himself a true romantic—a handsome (in his own opinion) soul who dreams of poetry and faraway lands. With the spirit of a wandering knight burning in his chest, he's sworn to sprint across every inch of Phantasia Mountain!

"Wild Charge!"

After reading a famous book called "A Knight's Tale," this goblin set out to be one too—starting with a noble steed. Alas, horses and goblin hips just don't mix... so a wild piglet will have to do!

"Imbecile! That's no boar—it's my steed of destiny!"

Although he managed to find a mount, riding it turned out to be far trickier than expected. But this clever goblin had a bright idea: why not dangle a carrot in front of the "horse"? Sure, steering's still a bit of a problem—but never mind the details! With that, his journey around the world began.

"A knight riding a pig? That's hilarious!" "So dumb—even worse than those two brothers... hah!" That kind of mockery hung over him every time he returned home. Most goblins might've been discouraged... but this one, fired up by countless tales of brave and noble knights, only grew more determined.

"True chivalry means staying humble in victory—and unshaken in defeat!"

Of course, the pursuit of chivalry is more important than the Ring of Dominion! Although he says that, it's hard not to be tempted by the ring's power. So, naturally, he charges headlong into battle, fighting as he goes. Even in combat, he insists on showing his enemies the proper dignity befitting a knight!

lore:
A sinister and arrogant dark elf assassin, ever lurking in the shadows, striking without warning from the veil of night. He works alone, scorning the world beneath the sun. Only profit and bloodshed hold his interest—both pursued with ruthless precision.

"Let's see... just how much you're worth to me."

Greedy for gold but lousy at saving, this sneaky scoundrel flips between petty theft and shady side gigs for others of its kind. Although inherently cunning, he often outsmarts himself and always ends up one step away from a tantrum.

"Curses! I've been bamboozled!"

Holds utter contempt for the wood elves, seeing them as nothing more than weaklings who cling to each other for safety. At night, often slips alone into their territory to steal and plunder—never once failing. Occasionally serves as a scout for larger dark elf warbands.

However, during a reconnaissance mission, he was spotted by a patrolling wood elf arrowslinger, and the two clashed in a fierce battle. Though he escaped in the end, he had never suffered such disgrace—and from that day forward, he bore a deep grudge against the wood elves.

Though he can't stand that arrogant Flamefiend, his grudge against the wood elves runs deeper. Out of spite, he joined the dark elves' war band—vowing to make the upcoming clash between the two races a painful lesson the forest folk won't soon forget.

"Wail and beg for mercy to your heart's content!"

title: Goddess of War
lore: Daughter of Zeus and Hera, Ares is the Goddess of War—the living embodiment of battle itself.

At times, Ares charges into battle atop a chariot drawn by four horses. Beside him ride his kin—Deimos, Phobos, Eris, and Enyo, embodiments of the terror, panic, strife, and destruction he brings to the battlefield.
Ares sees her sister Athena as her sworn rival, unable to accept that a shield-bearing defender could share the title "Goddess of War" alongside her.

Though Ares bears the title "Goddess of War," her record in battle is less than impressive. Arrogance and pride have cost her dearly, yet she refuses to yield. The more she is defeated, the stronger she becomes—and that, more than any title, is what makes her truly fearsome.
The moment Ares heard of Phantasia Mountain from Athena, she was eager to act. With Olympus already in disarray, her only desire was to add to the chaos.

summary: A low-health Warrior who deliberately sacrifices HP to gain shields and amplify his damage. [Crushing Fracture] creates Fissures that erupt after enough have accumulated, dealing heavy area damage, reducing Physical Defense, and instantly defeating non-elite summons. His {wild} state accelerates this payoff, while Trial's Blessing makes him increasingly durable as his HP falls.
title: Hercules
combat_tags: Godfist and Rebirth of Tempered Strength
lore:
Heracles is one of the main gods of Mount Olympus, renowned for his unparalleled Strength and unyielding resilience. He is the deity of Strength, Competition, Heroes, and protection in ancient Greece. As a figure who left immortal feats in the mortal realm, the underworld, and Mount Olympus, he symbolizes breaking free from fate, becoming the spiritual totem for mortals and Heroes in their battle against malevolence and injustice.


"I shall sing of Heracles, the son of Zeus, the unparalleled hero... Hail to you, O king, son of Zeus! Grant me virtue and happiness!" — The Homeric Hymn

Even as an infant, Heracles strangled the two serpents sent by the jealous Hera with her bare hands. This innate courage and Unyielding spirit bound her deeply to the image of "invincibility."

Hera's Curse imposed twelve seemingly impossible Trials upon her. She faced despair head-on, never backing down. It was precisely this overwhelming power and Indomitable Will that allowed her to stand tall amid the calamities of gods and mortals alike, becoming the Guardian deity of the Arena and the god of Redemption for the trapped. This is why she became the god of Heroes.

She is the only Hero who has broken through the boundaries of life and death with a mortal body. Hercules once entered the Underworld and faced the supreme majesty of Hades. Not only did he capture the Three-Headed Hound Cerberus to complete his trial, but he also shattered the eternal night Prison Cage for the tormented heroes.
She always adheres to the Hero's principles: witnessing the rise and fall of countless mortals and Heroes, but never using her supreme divine power to override the predetermined rules of fate. Only when injustice prevails and evil rampages will she deliver that crucial unstoppable punch to change the outcome.

"He once traveled across unspeakable lands and seas, obeying the orders of King Eurystheus. He committed many acts of violence himself and endured many hardships." — Homeric Hymns

Hercules possesses unparalleled divine strength and the courage to face his fate head-on. When Mount Olympus needs to quell unruly giants or purge the earth of malevolence, it always dispatches Hercules to the most perilous battlefields. He also once freed Prometheus Chained and joined the Argonaut Heroes in the search for the Golden Fleece. In every disaster between Mount Olympus and the mortal realm, the towering figure cloaked in lion skin is always seen standing at the forefront.

"Hercules, son of Zeus, the strongest hero among mortals and gods, you shall undertake those great deeds that no one dares to attempt, and purge the earth of its calamities." — 'The Iliad'

After reaching Phantasia Mountain, Heracles never ceased her protection of the trapped beings. Her steps traversed every perilous spot in this land, vanquishing the Marauder in the Maze and clearing paths blocked by the Forsaken Ice Fortress. In this brand-new world, she continues to write the immortal legend of the Hero and the Prime Guardian.
quote: I've had enough of the red tape on Mount Olympus.
ssr_quote: I was once a Hero in training... well, that was in the past.

title: Thunder Goddess
lore:
As one of the chief gods of the Aesir, Thor is both the strongest and the most forthright among the Norse gods, and the only one perpetually ready to fight the giants. As Odin's daughter, she willingly shoulders the duty of defending Asgard.

"As long as I stand here, the celestial palace will never fall."

Thor has always fought on the front lines against the giants. She once battled the World Serpent Jormungandr aboard a fishing boat, nearly crippling it. In Jotunheim's arena, she slew the frost giant Hrungnir with a single strike. At a wedding in Solemn, she faced a host of giants alone and defeated them all.

When Ragnarok arrives, Thor's opponent is her destined nemesis—the World Serpent, Jormungandr. The great serpent spews venom that corrodes Thor's body, while Thor strikes back, shattering its head with her hammer. This earth-shaking clash marks the opening of Twilight itself.

People regard Thor's hammer as sacred, composing epics to praise her defense of Asgard. This warrior, who fought the giants until the final moment, has long become a spiritual symbol of resistance against darkness.

"Thunder never fades. It only sleeps among the stars. When shadows again shroud the World Tree, the Thunder Goddess's hammer will tear the night apart."

Sensing the approach of a second Twilight, Thor arrived at Phantasia Mountain. This time, she vowed to stop Ragnarok from repeating and prevent the world's destruction.

"This time, I fight for the survival of Phantasia Mountain."
ssr_quote: Lesser gods must all bow to my will.

name: Andvari
summary: A shield-synergy Warrior who continuously generates self-shields whenever enemies are displaced, reducing her ultimate energy cost in the process. She excels at area-of-effect disruption, knocking up enemies and granting her team [Damage Boost] with [Dragon's Descent], and empowers her own attack by accumulating {black_dragons_claw} stacks through her shields.
title: Wings of Judgment
lore:
The Black Dragon Andvari was born from the embers of twilight and is one of the few dragons not corrupted by primordial venom.
During the cataclysm that burned everything to ash, the Black Dragon clan followed Nidhogg into battle against the gods, and was nearly annihilated. After the cataclysm, her mother found an ancient city to serve as a nest, providing refuge for the last remnants of the Black Dragon bloodline. Those were the only peaceful times for Andvari—her mother's wings shielding her from the chaos of the outside world.

The days of peace were fleeting. Rumors spread through the nearby mortal villages that a dragon guarded a vast hoard of treasure, and the hunt for the "evil wyrm" became a banner beneath which men pursued glory. At last, two youths, driven by greed, joined forces and stormed the lair. Her mother fell in battle, fighting to protect her. From that day on, Andvari became the last Black Dragon in the world. Across the long span of her life, only solitude and hatred remained at her side.

Hatred burned within her day and night. She withdrew to the desolate fringes of the world, sharpening fang and claw, gathering strength in silence. After years of lying in wait, she fixed her gaze upon one of her enemies—Nibelung, now the founding emperor of the Nilberg Empire.
Yet the assassination failed, and in its wake came relentless pursuit and calculated defamation. Nibelung recast her as the reincarnation of Nidhogg, an avatar of apocalypse; wherever her black wings were sighted, rumors of catastrophe followed. With no refuge left to her, Andvari vanished into the farthest reaches of desolation, severing herself from the world and walking alone within an eternity of solitude.

During her long years of seclusion, Andvari's hatred slowly yields to doubt. Cast aside and condemned by the world, she resolves to uncover the truth of history and pierce the veil of its distortions.
She crosses the endless void and reaches the Well of Hvergelmir. In its churning depths, she beholds the roots of the World Tree—and the unimaginable corruption spreading silently through them.

Now, Andvari's steps have halted at Phantasia Mountain. The scenes of Hvergelmir Spring have made her deeply question Nidhogg's motives for gnawing at the World Tree. She vows to uncover the buried past here and unearth the truth belonging to the Black Dragon clan.
quote: Fight with a dragon for too long, you'll become a dragon yourself.
ssr_quote: Gaze into the abyss too long, and the abyss will gaze back.

name: Arthur
summary: A supportive frontline Warrior who shares {fervor} with her allies and generates massive self-shields through [Breath of the King]. title: Eternal King
lore:
Daughter of King Uther, the great and everlasting ruler of Camelot. Dashing, gallant, and full of charm, she is known for her upright heart and shining chivalry, and is admired and revered by many. Guided by the great wizard Merlin, she gathered noble knights around her to form the Round Table—an order without rank or title, united in purpose, and devoted to the prosperity of Camelot. 

"Long live Camelot!"

Her birth was shrouded in dishonor—Uther Pendragon used deceit to father a child with the Duchess of Cornwall. The girl, Arthur, was sent away and raised in obscurity by a knight’s household, her early years marked by hardship and silence. Though she drew the sword from the stone, her claim was met with doubt and suspicion. But Merlin, who knew the truth of her bloodline, believed it was her fate to rule. With his guidance, she weathered the storm, forged a thriving kingdom from chaos, and, in time, won the hearts of her people.

With Merlin's guidance, the Lady of the Lake forged him a holy blade known as the Sword of Kings. Though its broad blade was sharp and mighty, it was the scabbard that bound his life and protected him. The people believed the young king would lead Camelot toward a radiant future. 

"All my strength exists to protect the realm."

For the sake of the kingdom's future, Arthur sought answers from the legendary Holy Grail, which revealed the existence of the Ring of Law. Though she ultimately claimed the ring, many knights of the Round Table sacrificed themselves in the process, and Lancelot's departure only deepened the King's troubles. The Ring of Law responded to her wish for newfound strength, but it brought not salvation—only renewed conflict. Alone, she faced endless enemies drawn by the ring's power, and the fire in her heart began to fade...

Following the Wild Hunt's plan, the Flamefiend struck at the opportune moment and destroyed the scabbard. Without its protection, King Arthur's unstable thoughts could no longer withstand the power of the ring—and he was consumed by it. With his fall inevitable, the Wild Hunt waited in the shadows to reclaim the ring for themselves. Camelot crumbled, hellfire devoured the land, and the kingdom's once-great glory turned to ash.

"Hope is lost. Honor, an illusion... What was I even fighting to protect...?"

name: Asmodeus
summary: A summon-synergy Warrior who empowers allied elite summons by granting them [Hellfire], turning them into massive sources of area-of-effect magic damage. She disrupts enemies by summoning [Imps] with [Demonic Reinforcements] and heals herself or her allies through [Infernal Dance] and by converting the damage dealt by her summons into health via [Thirst for Blood].
title: Demon Lord of Desire
lore: Asmodeus is one of the oldest demon lords of Hell and the embodiment of desire among the Seven Deadly Sins. For countless ages, she has silently observed the rise and fall of worlds. Unlike other demon lords driven by cruelty, she delights in weaving dreams—planting delusions in emperors' midnight thoughts and ambition in the dreams of beggars. All beings are actors upon her stage, and with a gentle pluck of desire's string, she can make the entire world dance.

She abandoned her role as a demon lord who wielded authority and became a pure observer. No longer weaving desire, she watched the choices born from it. She placed candy on an ant trail and lit a fire before it. The timid ants retreated. The clever ants detoured, only to collapse halfway. The most obsessed charged into the flames for a fleeting sweetness. This was Asmodeus's experiment, probing the eternal question of desire and human nature.

The monotony of day-to-day life left her weary, prompting her to ask herself what lay at the end of desire. As the source of desire, she had never once seen its endpoint in her followers. For that reason, she sealed her own memories and descended to the mortal world. She can no longer recall what happened during that time, but when she reclaimed her authority, she finally understood the nature of desire: it is never an endpoint, but the starting force that drives all existence.

Her greatest talent lies in letting desire grow naturally within the depths of the soul. Once, a sage famed for wisdom fell into an unhealthy obsession with knowledge under her whispers. Asmodeus never tempted him directly; she merely allowed him to glimpse a nonexistent "Codex of All Things" in his dreams. Chasing that illusion, the sage abandoned all his followers and spent his life lost in a labyrinthine library. This is her method—allowing desire to take root and bloom on its own.

Asmodeus followed her friend Gabriele to Phantasia Mountain and settled nearby. In her free time, she often sat quietly in a city tavern, observing the hidden desires of each patron without guiding them. Occasionally, when a glass ran dry, she granted a brief moment of clarity. She continued to wait, believing that one day someone might offer an answer beyond all expectation and bring her questions to an end.
quote: Would you like to form a pact with me?

title: Mighty Divine Bull
lore: Daughter of Queen Pasiphae of the Kingdom of Minos, once flourishing on the Aegean Sea. Born with a pair of horns, she was abandoned in the ancient Labyrinth on the island of Crete. A spirited girl who brandishes her giant axe and dashes through the maze with boundless energy. Though trapped within its endless corridors, she remains ever optimistic and kind, even seeing the Labyrinth as her true home.

According to survivors who once ventured into the Labyrinth and lived to tell the tale, the creature trapped within isn't the furious man-eating monster of legend, but a horned girl who warmly guides the lost—helping them evade deadly traps and find their way out.

Asteros has lived in the Labyrinth for as long as she can remember. Surrounded only by solitude, she spent her days growing up alongside the flowers and small creatures that shared her home. One day, she met several boys and girls who claimed to be from Athens—and through them, she learned for the first time of the world beyond the Labyrinth.

When the fully armed hero Theseus cautiously confirmed the girl's identity, he began to feel sympathy for the so-called "monster" whose name had spread far and wide. He led Asteros to the entrance of the Labyrinth, letting her decide for herself whether to step into the unknown world beyond.

Years later, having regained her freedom, Asteros arrived at Phantasia Mountain and embarked on her own adventure. Now, she can finally leave behind the towering walls of the Labyrinth and run freely once more.

title: Four Saints
lore: A young girl clad in battle armor, the dragon horn on her forehead marks her as the Azure Dragon Deity, guardian of the East. Under her command are the seven Eastern constellations, and her overwhelming strength places her at the top of the Four Saints.

The White Tiger, Azure Dragon, Vermilion Bird, and Black Tortoise are the Four Divine Beasts. Once celestial constellations, they absorbed the essence of heaven, earth, the sun, and the moon to become deities who protect the humans that revere them. The Azure Dragon often appears in spring, governing rainfall and serving as the most important god of agriculture, deeply tied to everyday life.

Whenever spring arrives, the Azure Dragon Deity sits watch over the East, ensuring favorable weather for the year's most crucial season of planting. Because of this responsibility, she holds a special fondness for winter, the only time of year when she can truly rest.

Though she appears aloof and distant, the Azure Dragon holds the deepest fondness for the mortal realm. In her leisure time, she often disguises herself as the wandering heroine known as the Azure Dragon Immortal Maiden, aiding the weak and upholding justice. The world believes this title is passed down through generations of master and disciple, yet for over a hundred years, every Azure Dragon Immortal Maiden has been her alone.

By a twist of fate, the Azure Dragon arrived at Phantasia Mountain. Seeing how factional strife had caused great suffering among the people, she felt a profound sense of responsibility. She vowed to restore peace to the mountain and protect the civilians—so they may have food to eat, clothes to wear, and a life of safety and well-being.
quote: Clouds Gather, Rain Falls, All Are Blessed.

title: Warborn Goddess
lore:
A divine and noble Warborn Goddess in service to Odin, King of the Gods, and a member of the einherjar host of Valhalla. Even among Warborn Goddesses, she is known as the strongest and most compassionate. Often seen riding her white steed across the skies, she gazes down upon the earth, her radiant shield reflecting the aurora as she brings courage and faith to every warrior below.

"The Warborn Goddesses are with you. The souls of the brave shall live on forever."

She once gently guided the souls of fallen warriors, lifting their confusion, honoring their courage, and leading them to the sacred halls of Valhalla. Yet her efforts could not prevent the coming of Ragnarok. Though her heart still holds deep affection for humanity, she now follows Valhalla's harsher doctrine—silently, and without question—determined to ensure such a calamity never happens again.

Though she maintains a valiant and dignified image before mortals, she is far from cold. On the contrary, she's deeply curious about human life and craftsmanship—often sneaking trinkets back to Valhalla, and secretly reading poems and books written about her. Perhaps it was this depth of feeling that once drew her into a complicated bond with the human hero Sigurd... though now, she avoids speaking of it altogether.

She often feels the crushing weight of duty on her shoulders, suppressing her emotions behind tireless duty. While other Warborn Goddesses occasionally rest, she never stops working. And yet, in the quiet moments between missions, a subtle loneliness follows her.

"My dreams matter far less than my duty... but if there really were a chance for them to come true..."

The betrayal of the Fallen Warborn Goddess and the rise of the Wild Hunt marked the coming of the apocalypse. Feeling her strength alone was no longer enough, she turned to the Ringsworn for aid. As she guided the party up Phantasia Mountain, she uncovered the Black Knight's true identity—but to her, personal feelings mattered less than the fate of the mountain itself. That was where her heart truly lay.

"No matter the cost... I will protect this world...!"

name: Hitomi
summary: A synergistic Warrior who forms a {link} with her highest-attack ally, granting mutual stat boosts and accumulating {nether_sight} stacks when they deal active skill damage. She unleashes devastating dash slashes with [Demonbane Flurry] and significantly empowers her linked ally's attack and defense once her {nether_sight} reaches maximum stacks.
title: Chaos Warlord
lore:
Hitomi, a warlord who rose from ruling a single province to dominate the entire Kinai region. After shattering the encirclement formed by various powerful warlords, she successfully advanced to Kyoto, took over the shogunate, and ultimately became the ruler of the entire Ashihara.
As a child, Hitomi was known among her subjects as the "Great Fool." She despised the constraints of outdated rituals and was dismissive of her studies, often causing her parents headaches with her rebellious nature. It wasn't until Hitomi personally led her troops to capture several cities in succession, with reports of victory pouring in, that people realized the military talent of this young lord was not to be underestimated.

After her first triumph, Hitomi inherited the mantle of family head from her father. Though still young, she already carried the bearing of a regional overlord.
What truly etched her name into the annals of Ashihara was a famed battle in which the few overcame the many. Having only just assumed leadership, she defied the objections of her retainers and personally led several hundred cavalry—banners inverted, hooves wrapped in cloth—down the riverbound cliffs in a sudden descent upon the enemy camp, shattering an army several times their number. In the wake of that crushing rout, her shaken foes bestowed upon her a fearful epithet: the Demon King of the Sixth Heaven.

Her ambition did not end there. Before long, she set her sights on a grander design: to bring all of Ashihara beneath her rule.
Thus began the sweeping march toward dominion. For years, the iron cavalry under her command rolled across the land like thunder. Cities capitulated at the mere rumor of her advance; enemy ranks faltered in dread. In the span of only a few years, she carved through Ashihara with unstoppable force, drawing the once-fractured realms beneath her banner and achieving a unification the world had never before witnessed.

Though Hitomi welcomed talent regardless of birth, she never found a successor who fully grasped her grand design. After unifying Ashihara, she resolved to enact her final reform—to prepare an age that would no longer require a hegemon.
Yet history turned sharply. Her most trusted general, long plotting in secret, launched a sudden assault at Nichiren Temple, setting it ablaze. In the inferno, Hitomi personally led her guard, reversed the tide, and struck down the rebel amid the flames—for she has always excelled at turning the few against the many.

After the battle at Nichiren Temple, Hitomi deeply realized that the road to reform was long and arduous. To seek the help of more like-minded individuals, she came to Phantasia Mountain. Now, she drinks and chats with various heroes here, and in her discussions and debates with others, she continues to search for a future for Ashihara that does not require a hegemon... a future that can prosper and endure without her.
quote: The path of the world needs no explanation.
ssr_quote: Fifty years in the mortal realm, like a dream, like an illusion...

She further sacrifices health to unleash area-of-effect attacks with [Blade Dance] and becomes significantly more lethal in the {wild} state, gaining massive Life Steal and increased damage for her skills.
title: Six-Armed Serpent
lore: A six-armed demigod serpent born in the distant past—proud, perilous, and utterly unbound by human morality. Obsessed with bloodshed and slaughter, she carved a fearsome path across the battlefield, vanquishing gods in a battle between dark creatures and the heavens. As punishment, she was cast into the underworld, condemned to bite only the wicked and the dying. Over countless ages, she built a gilded palace deep below the earth and filled it with strange and wondrous treasures...

Even after a thousand years, her thirst remained unquenched. Ever watchful of the world above, she finally found her way into the mortal realm through the underground waters that connect to the surface. Swearing vengeance on the gods who once persecuted her, she now hides among riverbeds and water weeds, claiming the lives of unsuspecting passersby with deadly poison. Though her power has waned, many of her serpentine kin still follow her.

Tales from every land speak of Marylis taking the form of a woman—bewitching mortals with her striking beauty. Sometimes she appears as a wealthy man's mistress, other times as a king's favored concubine. Across the ages, she feeds on human vitality and riches, mocking their foolishness and vanity, all while biding her time until her full power returns.

"Would you taste my poison? It's sweet as sugared frost..."

Even after draining the lives of countless humans, Marylis has yet to fully restore her power. Bored of the stagnation, she now longs for stronger opponents and greater devastation. When Flamefiend Ifrit invited her to join the Wild Hunt, she scoffed—unwilling to follow anyone's orders.

"Dominance and submission—that's the only kind of power that suits me. Leave those make-believe games to the kids."

Though not formally part of the Wild Hunt, Marylis keeps a close eye on their movements. Sensing that a great calamity is on the horizon, she can barely contain her excitement—hoping the chaos will help her fully restore her power. From the shadows, she sets her sights on the Ring of Dominion, biding her time.

"Ah yes... this ruinous, bottomless abyss... it's the only view I've ever longed to see."

title: Dragonslayer
lore:
The sole princess of Midham, the "kingdom under the mountain," and heir to the bloodline of the first hero, Sigurd. Bold, outspoken, and full of energy, she grew up on tales of Sigurd's legendary feats, and dreams of becoming a hero—a hero who will protect the people of Midham with sword in hand and heart ablaze.

"I'm a dragon-slaying hero AND a future king of legends! Well... almost."

Compared to her older brother Siegmund—the heir to the throne—Siegfried was given a far lighter curriculum in the royal palace. Even so, she skipped every etiquette class to sneak off and watch her brother train in the grand arena, secretly studying his swordplay. Thanks to her noble blood, natural talent, and relentless enthusiasm, her skills improved at a remarkable pace. Indulged by the king and impossible to rein in, the hot-blooded young fighter quickly earned a reputation as a fearless, untamable troublemaker.

Her older brother always forbade her from going to war, but Siegfried wasn't about to back down. Determined to prove herself, she ran away from home—leaving behind only a note. In the forest beyond the city, she captured a sprite named Viel and declared her a loyal sidekick. Though she was quickly dragged back home and scolded thoroughly, the taste of freedom had already lit a fire in the young princess's heart.

"I'm gonna save the whole world—so you'd better stick with me. There'll be meat to eat!"

No one foresaw Ladon's sudden attack. The city-state of Midham was consumed by flame. In the face of destruction, Siegfried remembered a family legend: the sealed dragon Fafnir, said to possess power enough to devour the World Tree. Siegfried swore to release it—but Prince Siegmund stood in her way, declaring that the fate of heroes and dragons has always been one of eternal conflict.

After Siegmund's death, Siegfried would occasionally lean on Ortros's broad back, reminiscing about his brother's strict teachings. The journey ahead remains perilous and uncertain, and the destined clash between hero and dragon may still await her. Yet for the sake of Midham—and the vow she made to protect it—courage always rises in her heart, undaunted and unshakable.

"Trust me, brother... I will sever the chains of fate with my own hands."
quote: Between you and me, it's irreconcilable!

title: Bloodthirster Sword
lore: Tyrfing, the Bloodthirsty Blade. Once drawn, it never misses, always draws blood, and is fated to one day slay its wielder.

Legend says the sword was forged by dwarves under threat of death, coerced by Odin's grandson. In their vengeance, the dwarves carved a curse into the blade upon its completion—sealing its fate, and the fate of all who would wield it.
After obtaining this sword, King Svafrlami met with victory after victory. Yet in a fateful battle against Arngrim, the blade slipped from his grasp—and in that moment, he was struck down.
After that, three successive wielders fell to the curse of the demon blade Tyrfing—and since then, the sword has vanished without a trace.

With chaos spreading across Phantasia Mountain, the people began praying for the rise of a hero and the return of a divine artifact to end their suffering. In this time of desperation, the Church of the Sacred Blade quickly rose to power, claiming to serve a single holy relic—the legendary sword, Gram.
quote: So much death, so much power.

summary: A resilient Warrior who enters the {wild} state to unleash a relentless [Savage Cyclone], continuously dealing area-of-effect physical damage to nearby enemies. He rapidly recovers lost HP upon entering the {wild} state using [Ancestral Will] and sacrifices his own health to materialize a spirit avatar that launches enemies into the air with [Heaven's Mandate].
title: Labyrinth Overlord
lore: Cursed from birth by the sea god Poseidon, Asteros is a bull-headed monster born of divine punishment. To keep its existence hidden, King Minos ordered Daedalus to construct an extraordinary labyrinth—one so complex that even Asteros itself could never find a way out.

To prevent the secret of the labyrinth from being revealed, King Minos imprisoned the craftsman Daedalus and his son Icarus within it alongside Asteros. The two eventually crafted wings from feathers they collected and made their escape by flying out of the maze.

When Minos's son Androgeus was slain in Athens, Minos prayed to the gods to punish the city. Seeking peace, the Athenians were forced to agree to a grim demand: every nine years, they would send seven boys and seven girls to Crete. In truth, these children were not a tribute to Minos—but a sacrifice, meant to feed Asteros.

Theseus, the son of King Aegeus of Athens, could not bear to see his people suffer such misfortune and decided to kill Asteros. He agreed with his father that if he returned with a black sail, it would mean he had died, and if he returned with a white sail, it would mean he had killed Asteros.
After arriving on the island of Crete, Theseus's charm and bravery caught the attention of King Minos's daughter, Ariadne. With the princess's help, Theseus ultimately defeated Asteros.

title: King of the Wild Hunt
lore: A powerful warrior clad in pitch-black armor, his entire body wreathed in spectral flames. Though his flesh has long since decayed, the war-hungry soul within refuses to rest.

The true identity of the Black Knight is none other than the King of the Wild Hunt. It is said that when the hunt passes through the mortal realm, it arrives with a roar like thunder. The people of Phantasia Mountain believe that anyone who witnesses its march with their own eyes is doomed to die.

Long ago, Beowulf defeated the night-fiend Grendel and his mother. With his own hands, he severed the monster's head and offered it to King Hrothgar of Heorot. Countless voices rose in praise as they gathered around him, hailing the great deed. In those days, Beowulf was still a hero.

However, few people know what Beowulf truly desires. He cares nothing for glory, craving only endless battle. As his aging body dragged him to the brink of death, realizing he may never fight again, Beowulf choose to stage one final fight... and perished alongside the wyrm.

To spread greater destruction, the Wild Hunt used a forbidden ritual to resurrect Beowulf. Returned as a spirit, he is no longer bound by age or mortality, yet this form of undeath has deeply warped his mind, magnifying the shadows in his heart. The Beowulf that walks the world now bears little resemblance to the hero of legend.


"I am eternal—undying."
quote: I have shed my mortal form.
ssr_quote: The armor and I have become one.

She focuses heavily on charging her [Iron Bulwark Shock] to deal massive area damage while granting {morale}, and excels at punishing shielded enemies by increasing her damage against them via [Shield‑Shattering Blade].
title: Heroic Warrior
lore:
Guna was the kingdom's most loyal and valiant warrior. She gave her life shielding her people during an enemy invasion—selfless, fearless, and remembered by all who knew her. After her death, she was taken to the heavens and reborn as a candidate for the Warborn Goddess.

"As the dawn sky split open, a thousand bells rang in unison; from the clouds, a bronze horn descended, and shattered blades and battered armor were bathed in divine radiance." — Oral Histories of Ancient Heroes

Guna was born the daughter of a minor noble on the frontier. From an early age, she trained with sword and spear on horseback, growing up beneath the open sky and listening to her father recount epic tales of heroes by the campfire. At fourteen, the enemy invaded. She watched with her own eyes as her father fell in battle, giving his life to protect the people of their land. With blood and tears still on her face, the young Guna took up her father's longsword, rallied the remaining soldiers, and held the fortress for seven days and nights.

"Your courage matches that of your father. Thus, I name you heir to your family's title. May you guard the frontier in my name, for all time."

Guna inherited not only the title of border nobility from her father but also the heavy burden that came with it. The enemy nation had long coveted the fertile land, yet Guna stood as an unyielding wall. However, the strongest defenses often crumble from within. That night, the enemy's army bypassed the sentries along the way, and the castle's drawbridge was secretly lowered. 

"The traitor sold their soul for a pitiful amount of money." — "Oral History of Ancient Heroes"

The last thing the survivors of that war saw was Guna turning back without hesitation, leading her royal guard to face the enemy alone—just as her father had once done. A warrior’s valor does not wither in the fires of war, nor does it falter before death.

On that blood-soaked field, a Valkyrie gathered her broken soul, and Odin forged her spirit anew. When Guna opened her eyes again, she stood in the halls of Valhalla—awaiting her next calling.

"Your courage is worthy of song. You are granted entry to Valhalla, freed from the mortal world, and counted among the gods."

Her legend now spreads across the land. It is said that Guna, Lota, and the youngest Goddess of Fate, Skadi, will ride to the battlefield to decide the outcome of battles and take away the souls of the fallen. 

"I say this is the twelfth. On the battlefield, Guna's horse saw the fodder, where twenty kings lay down." — "Rock Stele"
quote: I was chosen by Odin himself!

name: Siegfried
summary: A self-sustaining Warrior who gains massive Attack and Life Steal bonuses when attacking elementally-debuffed enemies through [Blazing Ambition]. She deals heavy area-of-effect physical damage and inflicts {ignite} with [Blazing Vortex], and enters the {wild} state to massively boost her defensive stats and overall attack power.
title: Hero Queen
lore:
The sole princess of Midham, the "kingdom under the mountain," and heir to the bloodline of the first hero, Sigurd. Bold, outspoken, and full of energy, she grew up on tales of Sigurd's legendary feats, and dreams of becoming a hero—a hero who will protect the people of Midham with sword in hand and heart ablaze.

"I'm a dragon-slaying hero AND a future king of legends! Well... almost."

Compared to her older brother Siegmund—the heir to the throne—Siegfried was given a far lighter curriculum in the royal palace. Even so, she skipped every etiquette class to sneak off and watch her brother train in the grand arena, secretly studying his swordplay. Thanks to her noble blood, natural talent, and relentless enthusiasm, her skills improved at a remarkable pace. Indulged by the king and impossible to rein in, the hot-blooded young fighter quickly earned a reputation as a fearless, untamable troublemaker.

Her older brother always forbade her from going to war, but Siegfried wasn't about to back down. Determined to prove herself, she ran away from home—leaving behind only a note. In the forest beyond the city, she captured a sprite named Viel and declared her a loyal sidekick. Though she was quickly dragged back home and scolded thoroughly, the taste of freedom had already lit a fire in the young princess's heart.

"I'm gonna save the whole world—so you'd better stick with me. There'll be meat to eat!"

No one foresaw Ladon's sudden attack. The city-state of Midham was consumed by flame. In the face of destruction, Siegfried remembered a family legend: the sealed dragon Fafnir, said to possess power enough to devour the World Tree. Siegfried swore to release it—but Prince Siegmund stood in her way, declaring that the fate of heroes and dragons has always been one of eternal conflict.

After Siegmund's death, Siegfried would occasionally lean on Ortros's broad back, reminiscing about his brother's strict teachings. The journey ahead remains perilous and uncertain, and the destined clash between hero and dragon may still await her. Yet for the sake of Midham—and the vow she made to protect it—courage always rises in her heart, undaunted and unshakable.

"Trust me, brother... I will sever the chains of fate with my own hands."

lore: In Norse mythology, dwarves were born from the flesh and blood of Ymir, the primordial giant. Perhaps the fiery red hair and beard of Grimnir are echoes of that ancient origin—a lingering trace of the blood that once flowed through the father of giants.

Grimnir once invited the most renowned rune master of the dwarves to inscribe sacred runes upon his body. The process was said to cause excruciating, bone-deep pain—but not once did Grimnir utter a sound.
Grimnir is a highly respected Berserker of the Dwarven Kingdom. Once he sets foot on the battlefield, he does not stop fighting until either his enemies lie dead—or he does.
Although most of his life has been spent on the battlefield, Grimnir knows how to enjoy the quieter moments. He often visits taverns—not to drink, but to sit in silence and listen to the bards sing.

Phantasia Mountain is no longer the peaceful place it once was. Monsters and beasts roam unchecked, and the Wild Hunt is brewing a shocking conspiracy. It was in this brewing storm that Grimnir first heard the tale of the Ringsworn.

lore:
The lowest-ranking demon in all of Hell, often found serving under the Flamefiend and running errands for higher-ranking devils. Lacking the strength or status to cause real trouble, it mostly handles grunt work.

"Don't underestimate me! Even peon demons are still demons!"
Though of low rank, Murphy has the dubious honor of serving directly under the Flamefiend. After all, when the Flamefiend feels the need, Murphy makes for a surprisingly decent chair.

It is said that those who are tempted by demons and sign a pact with them will, upon death, have their souls dragged into the depths of hell. There, unquenchable hellfire reshapes them into the lowest rank of demon.

"Work hard! There's a promotion system in hell too!"

Murphy has served the Flamefiend for a long time—never praised and barely noticed. In the end, he's little more than a footrest. Though he doesn't dare complain aloud, his diary is another story. He's even placed curses on those who've tried reading it without his permission.

After the Flamefiend joined the Wild Hunt, Murphy followed loyally to Phantasia Mountain. But after witnessing the Ringsworn and his party repeatedly foil his boss's schemes... he started to consider switching sides.

name: Goblin Battering Ram
summary: A sacrifice-based Warrior who deals massive single-target damage with [Siegebreaker], which scales with his current HP, before instantly dying. Upon death, he spawns two Goblin Clubbers that inherit his stats and gain {excitement}, ensuring continued offensive pressure.
lore:
Unlike a certain pair of silly brothers, this goblin is disciplined, battle-ready, and (in his own words) totally cool. With unshakable spirit and a love for battlefield glory, he's sworn to win every war across Phantasia Mountain, one fortress at a time.

"Heave-ho! Heave-ho!"

Goblin battering rams operators are trained in pairs, a role that demands a level of coordination most goblins famously lack. To build that bond, they grow up together from an early age—eating, sleeping, slacking off, whitewater rafting, dodging traps, and surviving adventurer attacks side by side. With a life like that, it's no surprise they've developed an unshakable sense of teamwork.

"Charge! Aaah!"
"W-Wait for me! You shouted too fast!"
Even the most in-sync goblins are prone to the occasional squabble—whether it's over how to shout a battle cry, what lines to yell, or who gets to stand in front. Their movements may be perfectly coordinated, but their personalities remain wonderfully, stubbornly unique.

"A goblin's individuality is like a radiant, solitary flower in full bloom." —Field Notes on Goblins of the Phantasia Mountains

"A foot soldier playing at being a general?" "So dumb—even worse than those two brothers... hah!" That kind of mockery hung over him every time he came home. Most goblins might have lost heart—but one burning with the spirit of battle only grows stronger.

"To live for a single moment—that's the true essence of battle!"

Of course, the upcoming battle is more important than the Ring of Dominion! ...Or so he says. Still, it's hard for him not to get a little distracted by the ring's rumored power while fighting. So now, between bashing enemies and dodging fireballs, he finds himself thinking about it more often than he'd admit. Anyway, it's time to show everyone what a battle-hardened goblin is really made of!

title: Sun Goddess
lore:
Apollo, the Daughter of Light, the embodiment of music and prophecy. She is also the god of medicine and livestock. Upholding justice and virtue, she leads humanity forward. 

"Apollo’s golden hair is crowned with laurel leaves from Mount Parnassus. Her purple robe sweeps the ground, and her lyre, inlaid with gems and Indian ivory, rests in her left hand as she plucks the strings with his right." — Ovid, Metamorphoses

Whenever night draws to a close, the goddess of dawn awakens in the east, rising to open the gates of Apollo's radiant palace. As the stars retreat into the fading darkness, Apollo ascends the sky in his sun chariot, drawn by four celestial steeds, casting light and warmth upon all creation.

"A palace vast and glorious, its lofty columns reaching the heavens, gleaming with gold and burning with bronze. Its high eaves were laid with ivory white, and its twin gates shone with silvery light." — Ovid, Metamorphoses

Young Apollo, holding a lyre and carrying a silver bow, runs through the azure sky, with golden arrows clinking in the quiver. She rushes to the cave where the giant serpent Python resides, seeking revenge for her mother Leto. Her golden arrows, always hitting their mark, rain down on Python, who breathes his last. Apollo sings a triumphant victory song.

Because Apollo killed Python, she was punished to herd livestock, using hard labor to atone for her sins. She played the flute and lyre on the pasture, and the beasts enchanted by her music emerged from the Dense Forest. Leopards and wild lions moved gently among the flock, while wild deer and antelopes danced to the rhythm of the flute. A peaceful and joyful atmosphere surrounded them.

Legendary tales say that whenever there is a plea, Apollo will go to resolve people's calamities. She is powerful, yet compassionate. Perhaps having heard the prayers, this deity has now arrived at Phantasia Mountain.

She grants the {darkmoon} state to allied ranged Luminaries with [Darkmoon Embrace], increasing their skill haste and damage, while automatically retaliating against attackers using [Owl Leap].
title: Goddess of the Moon
lore: The moon goddess and goddess of the hunt of Olympus, daughter of Zeus and the Titaness Leto, and twin sister of Apollo. At the age of three, Artemis asked her father for eternal chastity, twenty Oceanid nymphs as attendants, and dominion over forests and cities. Zeus granted her wishes and further appointed her guardian of continents and islands, letting her silver light shine across land and sea.

Artemis often roams forests beneath the moon, bow in hand. She once governed only the fate of hunters and beasts, but as her followers prayed beneath moonlight, she gained lunar authority. She became the New Moon aspect of the Triune Moon Goddess.

"The air at the zenith is the purest, farthest from the tainted world. The Moon Goddess changes form—growing during the waxing phase and shrinking during the waning." — Ovid, Metamorphoses

In the giant war that shook Mount Olympus, one of the most powerful and arrogant giants, Porphyrion, set his sights on Hera. At the critical moment, a streak of silver light tore through the battlefield—Artemis's divine arrow pierced the giant's chest, defeating him alongside the mortal hero Heracles. With the wrath of the Moon Goddess, Artemis safeguarded Olympus's dignity and won the gods a chance to turn the tide of fate.

During the Trojan War, the Greek commanders angered Artemis. She stilled the sea winds, trapping the fleet in harbor, and declared that only the sacrifice of a maiden could appease her wrath. Yet before the ritual, she showed mercy, shrouding the girl in mist and substituting a deer in her place.

"The goddess received her due sacrifice. Her wrath subsided, and with it, the sea's fury faded." — Ovid, Metamorphoses

During a routine patrol, the divine deer suddenly lifted its head and cried out, scattering birds across the sky. Artemis sensed Apollo's presence. The stag's warnings never fail. Her gaze sharpened as she grasped her silver bow and headed toward Phantasia Mountain, uncertain which fate her arrows would pierce next.

title: Spellbreaker Miko
lore:
Himiko, the Queen of Yamatai, is renowned for her ability to commune with spirits and interpret divine will, earning her fame as a Miko. Skilled in pacifying the world through her practices, she acts under the divine mandate of Takamagahara and was chosen by the war-torn tribes of the archipelago as their ruler. She governs the prosperity and stability of her nation and ensures the Vitality and peace of its people.
Himiko possesses deep insight into human nature, using divine will to mediate tribal conflicts and establish the principles of Divine Order. She also brings Soothe to displaced citizens through her benevolence. With the purity and dignity of a Miko, she unites the fragmented tribes of the archipelago into a resilient kingdom capable of withstanding chaos and maintaining stability.

In the hearts of countless people of Yamatai, some revere her as the untouchable emissary of the divine. She consistently channels the will of heavens, spirits, and gods, uncovering the root of chaos and decisively ending disputes with unquestionable judgement. Others respect her as a benevolent mother to the populace. Not only does she dispel disease and calamity through rituals, but she also prepares safe havens and sustenance for displaced people.
What she seeks to bestow upon the masses has never been merely the hollow stability offered by divine protection. It is the understanding that behind this tranquility lies a homeland worth guarding with their hearts and lives.

Himiko upholds the creed of stabilizing the turbulent times and protecting all people with benevolence, almost obsessively ensuring that every tribe on the archipelago is free from war and every household can live in peace and security.
Upon learning that the male king of Kunukoku, Himikoyumo, had raised an army to invade, throwing the archipelago into the brink of war once again, the entire Yamatai kingdom was engulfed in panic. Only the people under Himiko's rule steadfastly held onto their belief in mutual support and reliance. The citizens remembered the years of peace brought by the queen, and the shouts of border guards reverberated through the straits, shaking even the waves and winds.

Himiko dedicated her life to ending the century-long strife on the archipelago. Near the end of her life, she passed the throne to her niece Kazane and passed away amidst the lingering melodies of Kagura.
Her soul, trapped in the ancient homeland of Yamatai, bestowed divine omens but could not restore the lost hearts of the people. She eventually realized that while she could establish Divine Order for a time, she could not eradicate the endless cycle of Reincarnation and strife. When the ocean winds carried away the final notes of her prayers, this queen who had devoted her life to her nation shed scalding tears for the countless lives she could not protect.

Witnessing the endless cycle of war in her homeland, Himiko finally severed her attachment to mortal dynasties, crossing the boundary of life and death to traverse various realms, eventually finding solace in Phantasia Mountain.
Here, there are no distinctions of rank or tribe, only souls bound by their past obsessions and crushed by fate on the same journey. At this moment, she is no longer the exalted Elven Queen of Yamatai nor the Miko attempting to reverse the chaos in the mortal world. With the power of sorcery, she listens to obsessions and soothes scars, transforming herself into a beacon of light. She shines a path forward for every lost soul, helping them find an eternal sanctuary of peace.
quote: Let me be the one to dispel your resentment!
