title: Twin Ravens
lore:
A strange girl never seen without her talkative raven companion. She rarely speaks, leaving the chatter to the bird at her side, who eagerly voices her thoughts and requests. Known for her sharp intellect, she prefers to observe from the shadows, quietly watching the world unfold. 

"Quiet down a little, Huginn. I'm thinking."

It is said that the God King Odin is often accompanied by two ravens, one named Huginn and the other Muninn. They are Odin's raven gods, leaving at dawn each day to observe events unfolding around the world, and returning at night to report to him, whispering in his ear while perched on his shoulder. Thanks to their presence, no change or movement in the world can escape the eye of Odin.

They share a single soul, divided between two bodies. Huginn bears memory—gifted with perfect recall, he speaks only of what has truly come to pass, often repeating the same words over and over. Muninn bears thought—discerning meaning and offering counsel, especially to Odin, whom they serve alone. Their unwavering loyalty to him has stirred the ire of other gods. It is said their soul was sundered in two as an act of divine vengeance.

Although Muninn, the epitome of thought, is also a raven, she chose to take a human form, guided by her sharp sense of self. But the two still share a soul, and without Huginn's support, she tends to space out. Their minds are linked, and to preserve her poised, intellectual image, she often has him speak on her behalf. 

"...I wasn't daydreaming. Huginn just left for a moment."

Once proud to serve as Odin's eyes and ears, they still revere the fallen Allfather, awaiting the day of his return. Yet in their newfound freedom, they've come to enjoy the unshackled life—driven by their innate thirst for knowledge, observing and remembering all they see, just as they once did. One day, that knowledge may once again prove useful. 

"Remember it all, Huginn. That's my final judgment."
quote: No one can escape my eyes.

title: Flamefiend
lore:
A demon born of fire, wielding complete control over flame. Cruel by nature, she is cunning, arrogant, and utterly destructive, reveling in chaos and unrest. As a vanguard of the Wild Hunt, she follows the orders of the Black Knight, sowing discord and disaster wherever she goes. The havoc she unleashes isn't just a mission—it's her twisted delight.

"Just imagining humanity's panicked screams on doomsday... sends chills up my spine!"

Historically, she was known for sparking fires at random, luring mortals into crime and chaos, and dragging kings and leaders into the depths of darkness. Even gods and angels were not spared from her capricious meddling. Like flame itself, her nature was wild and unpredictable. Since joining the Wild Hunt, her actions have taken on a strange sense of order. Fearful of the Flamefiend, some humans have begun to worship her, hoping in vain to escape destruction—but to her, their pleas are nothing more than the dying struggles of insects.

Countless mages through the ages have tried to craft sigils to control her—but the Flamefiend, who delights in disaster, only yields to those stronger than herself. She follows the Black Knight partly out of respect for his power, and partly because the Wild Hunt's chaos happens to suit her tastes. But in truth, she cares little for the group's goals. She's far more interested in her own enjoyment—and gets along poorly with the others.

"Tch... This bunch of weaklings can't even keep things interesting."

The Black Knight saw chaos in the Flamefiend's heart and invited her to join the Wild Hunt. Knowing the Ring of Law's power well, she eagerly followed his orders to collect the Rings of Law. Her first target was the fire ring, held by the Goddess of Fate. Using venom to strike at the source, she dulled their foresight and stole the ring—unleashing chaos with newfound power.

Like the Wild Hunt, she seeks the power of the Ring of Dominion. Even when her plans are disrupted by the Ringsworn Legion, she finds herself exhilarated. Whatever fate may bring, she intends to revel in the chaos to the very end.

"Does a moth fly into the flame out of courage—or ignorance? Either way... it always burns."

title: Crimson Thornblade
lore: Jing is an Assassin. Since she can remember, she has been by her master's side, honing her assassination skills day after day. Finally, on the day she came of age, her master handed her five short blades, telling her that her mission was to be the measure of the world, to assassinate unjust deities, and to maintain the rights of mortals.

At that time, Jing did not have a name. She always aimed to defeat her master, observing him daily and applying her insights in actual combat, with significant results. When she believed she had identified her master's greatest weakness, she invited him to spar, only to find that his techniques were completely different from before. Once again, she was defeated by her master. 

The master placed a red ribbon over her eyes and told her, "As an assassin, you must never trust anyone in your life—not me, not even yourself."

With her eyes covered, Jing gradually learned to observe with her heart. Finally, on a rainy day, she defeated her master. She heard her master's sigh but didn't know why he sighed, nor did she dare to ask. She buried the joy of victory deep in her heart, not daring to show a trace.

From that day on, she officially bore the name "Jing," a recognition from her master and proof of her graduation.

On the day Jing came of age, her master solemnly handed her a large box. 

Inside the box were five short blades, representing the responsibility of generations of "Jing." These five short blades were crafted by mortal craftsmen, nameless yet possessing the power to end the lives of deities. 

From this moment on, Jing would use these five nameless short blades to maintain the interests of mortals. Jing accepted the short blades and also took on this responsibility.

After leaving her master, Jing has been traveling through the Nine Realms. She has become accustomed to covering her eyes, which allows her to sense people's hearts with greater clarity and reduces the vigilance of her "enemies." The Nameless Scabbard has always been by her side, waiting to drink the blood of evil gods.
quote: Right and wrong, good and evil, all follow one heart.
ssr_quote: The daylight pierces, yet none can see.

title: Mother of Serpents
lore:
A terrifying serpent-haired gorgon whose long locks are made entirely of writhing pythons. She is even known to speak with them on occasion. She possesses the power to turn living beings to stone, treating the resulting statues as precious toys and prized collectibles. She dwells deep within a damp, shadowy palace, lying in wait for unsuspecting prey. For reasons unknown, her hostility toward men is especially intense.

"What a beautiful little thing you are... I'll take such good care of you."

Obsessively devoted to her own beauty, she applies phosphorescent powder as makeup and washes her face with serpent venom each day. Consumed by jealousy toward Athena's radiance, she kills any human who dares speak against her appearance. Even her sisters—Stheno and Euryale—fear her wrath. As servants of Hades, the three Gorgon sisters are known and dreaded by that name alone—serpent-haired beings whose gaze and fury few survive.

The Gorgon Maidens are descendants of the Olympian gods. One side of their blood is poison, while the other holds the power to bring the dead back to life. Thus, Stheno and Euryale possess immortal bodies, untouched by time. But Medusa was once human. After her death, her corpse was infused with serpent's blood, reborn as one of her sisters' kind. Because of this, she remains the only Gorgon who is not truly immortal.

After transforming into her serpent-like form, Medusa's personality changed entirely. Gone was the innocence she once had as a human. She grew obsessed with adding to her "collection," preying on countless humans—even the heroes sent to slay her. This caught Athena's attention. The goddess sent a vision to Perseus, urging him to destroy her—but in response, Medusa only laughed.

"Come, let me add you to my collection... I still want more—more!"

The overwhelming power of the Queen of the Underworld won the devotion of the three sisters—Medusa most of all. Enraptured by the pleasure of corruption, she carries out her will without question. Yet when she set her sights on killing Perseus, he calmly proposed a deal. As it turns out, what he truly sought was not victory—but blood that could raise the dead.

"Gaze upon me, mortals... and see for yourselves how beautiful I truly am!"

title: Giant of Wisdom
lore: Mimir is the Giant of Wisdom who perceives the essence of all things and the master of the Spring of Wisdom. She is not a guardian of knowledge, but knowledge in motion itself. At first, the metaphysical laws of the world intoxicated her. She rejoiced at creation and wept at destruction. But when cognition reached its boundless end, the weave of fate became an unalterable map in her eyes. She foresaw every falling dewdrop, every life's trajectory, and even the end of the gods. All things drift upon predetermined paths, without exception.

Omniscience brought Mimir not fulfillment, but vast emptiness. This void endured until Odin appeared. The king of the gods offered any price for a drink from the Spring of Wisdom. Mimir demanded one of his eyes. Odin agreed without hesitation. Thus, Odin gained the spring's wisdom and learned of the coming Ragnarok.

Soon after, war erupted between the Vanir and the Aesir, and Mimir paid a terrible price. Her physical body was destroyed by the Vanir, while her consciousness was confined beside Odin until the war ended. This humiliation awakened her to a truth: wisdom, like a weapon, draws its value not from possession, but from how it is wielded.

When Ragnarok's horn echoed across the skies, Mimir alone saw a chance within the catastrophe. As the World Tree convulsed and all eyes turned to the battlefield, she escaped Odin's side, returned to the Spring of Wisdom, and used its power to rebuild her body.

The renewed Spring of Wisdom surged with power beyond comprehension—shattered divinity, lost civilizations, and unwritten epics. When the fallen Warborn Goddess plunged into its depths, Mimir glimpsed a truth in an instant: frozen destinies were restarting. This time, she did not merely observe. She reached out her hand, inviting the fallen to walk alongside her toward the ultimate paradise.
quote: I have unraveled the secrets of the spring.

title: Corrupted Bloom
lore:
She is a new sprout born beside the Hvergelmir spring of the World Tree Drasill, named Ningrose by the gods, meaning "white blossom." On the day Nidhogg gnawed through the main root, its venom crept up her bud along the growth rings. Venom and sap coexisted within her veins, and she heard herself begin to pulse across countless parallel worlds.

"As long as Vidofnir still sings upon your treetop, you can spread vitality to all realms." — Odin's Blessing

Ningrose is gentle and curious by nature, wishing only for each leaf to catch the morning light. After Nidhogg's corruption seeped in, her buds darkened and reeked of iron. On the ruins of Twilight, she entwined fallen warriors with her roots for the first time, turning their bodies into nourishment. That night, she carved a whistle from a branch, sounding a deathly call that lured enemies into the mist. The wind carried the notes across the Nine Realms, and even the stars closed their eyes.

Upon the Norn Goddess's corrupted threads of fate, the chronicler leaves this conclusion for her: some say she was broken by the flames of Twilight, swept into the sky by Surtr's fire and turned into a comet that burned through the Nine Realms; some say she broke free from the World Tree, fell back into Niflheim, and grew into an inverted iron thorn by the poison spring, piercing even the Black Dragon's spine; colder ballads whisper that she used the World Tree's connections to spread corruption to every world.

Ningrose ultimately returned to the roots of the World Tree, awaiting complete corruption. Yet when she touched the roots, she beheld an unexpected vision—herself in another world, living an entirely different life. Fate's final cruelty shattered her completely, and she became the embodiment of decay. From then on, she used the World Tree as a bridge to spread corruption from one world to the next.

Now reborn as a corrupted bud, she relived countless possibilities through the World Tree's connections. She saw herself discovered early by Odin and struck down by the Eternal Spear, triggering Ragnarok ahead of time. She saw the Nine Realms consumed by ice and fire, where she rotted alone upon frozen ground. In every world, the ending was the same. As visions flowed through her mind, the outline of Phantasia Mountain grew clearer. Somewhere beyond reason, she sensed that this time might be the final chapter.
ssr_quote: Nothing can avert the fate of decay.

title: Froststar Hunter
lore:
She is the sharp arrow in the frost and snow, the piercing sound in the air. Wherever her ice arrows fall, no life remains. And yet, even with such power, her heart remains bound to vengeance.

"There will be no peace... until my revenge is complete."

A monstrous serpent that spews venom and leaves wastelands in its wake wherever its massive body slithers. The more it hears the screams of the terrified, the redder its eyes burn with fury.

"Wasn't it supposed to stay beneath the surface...? How did this happen?"
With a frost crossbow on her back and hatred as her arrows, those days of peace are long gone for this girl. Between humans and monsters, there was never room for coexistence.

She had tracked the serpent for months. Teammates came and went. Exhaustion swept over the whole party. Maybe giving up was wiser—at least, that's what everyone else said.

"They had nothing to lose. But I... I'm different."

The moment she loosed the crossbow bolt at the girl, she felt no joy. She knew the shot would land. There would be blood. The monster would die. But vengeance, as it turns out, carries no warmth. Only cold.
quote: The time for revenge has come!

title: Radiant Elemental
lore:
An elemental being born of pure light, rarely seen by human eyes. She spends most of her time hidden from view, her golden glow giving off a gentle, calming presence. Though seemingly carefree, she works tirelessly under orders from above—and has accumulated more than a few complaints that never quite make it into the official report.

"Emitting light particles counts as fine-grained alignment, right...? Ugh, what am I even talking about?!"

She once dwelled within a distant elemental plane, gifted with the power to move between worlds. Over countless years, she gradually took on human form, carrying with her the quiet hope of bringing light to the world. Now, she watches silently over those lost in darkness, offering guidance without ever asking for thanks.

"Do not be afraid—there is always a light that can pierce the darkness and lead the way to hope."

The Goddess of Fate called upon the light spirit to walk with them, and sensing their ability to see the truth of all things, she chose to accept, descending into the world. Perhaps it was destiny—or simply a desire to make the world a better place. Yet like all bright-eyed newcomers stepping into their first job, she soon found herself worn down by endless errands and unexpected trials.

Though the Goddess of Fate remain neutral in their judgment and rarely interfere directly with the world, they have voiced concerns about those who have fallen into darkness. Still, her relationship with her superiors remains civil. Even if she doesn't always understand the goddesses' intentions... if it's an order from above, then surely there must be a reason for it... Probably.

Although it turned out quite different from what she initially envisioned, her inherently optimistic nature has adapted to this life. It seems that becoming a comic relief character might just be part of fate's grand design. But with a new crisis looming over Phantasia Mountain, how could a subordinate of the Goddess of Fate simply sit still and do nothing? Then again... is that really something a mere overworked assistant gets to decide?

"You've got this, you gorgeous semi-naked assistant, you! Okay, daily self-motivation complete—time to get to work."
quote: May this light illuminate your path.
ssr_quote: I am the embodiment of light.

title: Gorgon
lore:
A terrifying serpent-haired gorgon whose long locks are made entirely of writhing pythons. She is even known to speak with them on occasion. She possesses the power to turn living beings to stone, treating the resulting statues as precious toys and prized collectibles. She dwells deep within a damp, shadowy palace, lying in wait for unsuspecting prey. For reasons unknown, her hostility toward men is especially intense.

"What a beautiful little thing you are... I'll take such good care of you."

Obsessively devoted to her own beauty, she applies phosphorescent powder as makeup and washes her face with serpent venom each day. Consumed by jealousy toward Athena's radiance, she kills any human who dares speak against her appearance. Even her sisters—Stheno and Euryale—fear her wrath. As servants of Hades, the three Gorgon sisters are known and dreaded by that name alone—serpent-haired beings whose gaze and fury few survive.

The Gorgon Maidens are descendants of the Olympian gods. One side of their blood is poison, while the other holds the power to bring the dead back to life. Thus, Stheno and Euryale possess immortal bodies, untouched by time. But Medusa was once human. After her death, her corpse was infused with serpent's blood, reborn as one of her sisters' kind. Because of this, she remains the only Gorgon who is not truly immortal.

After transforming into her serpent-like form, Medusa's personality changed entirely. Gone was the innocence she once had as a human. She grew obsessed with adding to her "collection," preying on countless humans—even the heroes sent to slay her. This caught Athena's attention. The goddess sent a vision to Perseus, urging him to destroy her—but in response, Medusa only laughed.

"Come, let me add you to my collection... I still want more—more!"

The overwhelming power of the Queen of the Underworld won the devotion of the three sisters—Medusa most of all. Enraptured by the pleasure of corruption, she carries out her will without question. Yet when she set her sights on killing Perseus, he calmly proposed a deal. As it turns out, what he truly sought was not victory—but blood that could raise the dead.

"Gaze upon me, mortals... and see for yourselves how beautiful I truly am!"

title: Demon Hunter
lore: It's said that the famed demon hunter Van Helsing arrived in the Phantasia Mountain in pursuit of a bloodthirsty werewolf. But even a seasoned tracker like her must first study unfamiliar terrain before she can resume the hunt.

To better adapt to life on Phantasia Mountain, Van Helsing stepped out of the shadows and joined the Adventurer's Association. He began engaging with the locals, learning their ways, and training alongside them. Now, through daily practice and discipline, his combat skills have grown even sharper.

Van Helsing was born into an ancient and mysterious family, with generations bearing the mission of protecting humanity from dark forces in the shadows. As he grew, Van Helsing gradually mastered swordsmanship, firearms, combat, pharmacology, monsters, and various spells.
Evidently, hard work pays off, and Van Helsing finally found the trail of the werewolf. As she cautiously approached the target, she was surprised to see a young girl with animal ears and a tail.

The cat-eared girl's appearance didn't fool Van Helsing. After a period of quiet surveillance, he temporarily ruled her out as his target. And yet... the strange scent she carries continues to raise his suspicions. For now, the truth remains unresolved.

title: Savage Hunter
lore: A spear-wielding centaur with the lower body of a zebra. In the blue-green landscape of Phantasia Mountain, their black-and-white stripes offer no camouflage at all—if anything, they stand out even more.

Nessus considers himself the finest hunter in the Phantasia Mountains. Unlike other centaurs who charge their prey at full speed, he prefers to strike from a distance, hurling his spear with deadly precision. And to his credit, his aim is near flawless, almost never missing his mark.
Though known as a brutal and savage centaur, Nessus once lived a brief period of peace. Fleeing his homeland, he came to the River Evenus, where he worked for many years as a ferryman.

However, when the great Hero Heracles arrived at the river with his wife, intending to cross, the centaur Nessus laid covetous eyes on her. Heracles shot him with a poisoned arrow, but before dying, Nessus whispered a lie to the hero's wife—one that would one day lead to Heracles's own death.

When he opened his eyes again, Nessus found himself on Phantasia Mountain for some unknown reason. Viewing this "rebirth" as a new opportunity, he made up his mind—he would become the greatest hunter the mountain had ever seen—one whose name would strike fear into all who heard it!

title: Cyclops
lore: Polyphemus is a cyclops from Greek mythology, born of the sea god Poseidon and the sea nymph Thoosa. Towering and immensely strong, he bears a single eye on his forehead and is said to dwell in a massive cave on the island of Sicily.

Though towering in strength, the one-eyed giant Polyphemus is notoriously dim-witted. When Odysseus blinded him, he tricked the giant by giving his name as "Nobody." So when Polyphemus cried out that "Nobody is attacking me," the other giants assumed he was unharmed—and no one came to his aid.
Though cyclopes are often seen as crude and dim-witted, they are master builders by trade. With ease, they move massive stones and construct structures beyond the imagination of ordinary mortals.

After years of heavy lifting, the cyclopes has even developed a skill for throwing. With their immense strength, they can hurl boulders with terrifying precision and enough power to crush anything in their path.

Although Cyclops has a violent temperament, is also surprisingly playful, and is especially fond of plump, fast-moving creatures like wild boars. He apparently finds them endlessly entertaining... Who knows, maybe one day he'll try using a boar as a living projectile.
ssr_quote: A single eye and a mighty horn!

name: Dwarven Cannoneer
summary: An ammo-based Archer who consumes bullets with her basic attacks to deal area-of-effect physical damage through her [Barrel Up] talent. She deals extra damage to enemies with high Overdrive costs and unleashes massive explosive damage in a small area using [Blazing Barrel].
lore:
Dwarven cannoneers serve as ranged units within the dwarven army. Unlike other races that favor bows and arrows, the dwarves prefer firepower—choosing cannons for their superior range and destructive force.

"Times have changed, lads! Let's have a blast!"

Cannons pack far more power than bows, and that applies to both enemies and allies. A poorly aimed shot can just as easily hit friendlies as foes. That's why every dwarven cannoneer undergoes formal training before ever setting foot on the battlefield—just to make sure they don't end up aiming the barrel the wrong way.

Dwarves are a mountain-dwelling race, known for building their cities deep within hollowed-out peaks. To better shatter the rock, they invented gunpowder—and before long, cannons for war soon followed. The appearance of dwarven cannoneers, armed with these powerful new weapons, once stirred fear among the other races.

However, this panic did not last long. The turmoil on Phantasia Mountain quickly sent the once-prosperous dwarven kingdom into decline. Many master craftsmen were lost in the chaos, and the knowledge of crafting gunpowder and cannons faded with them. These days, the cannons wielded by dwarven cannoneers are not new creations, but relics of a bygone age.

Once proud members of the dwarven army, dwarven cannoneers have earned great merit in countless battles, helping secure victory after victory for their kingdom. But times have changed. Now, many operate as mercenaries across Phantasia Mountain—hired by various factions, and in some cases, even lending their firepower to the Wild Hunt.

name: Wood Elf Archer
summary: A rapid-firing Archer who significantly boosts her Attack Speed by consuming {awakening} stacks via [Blessing of the Elves]. She deals heavy physical damage to a single target with [Burst Fire] and targets an area with [Cloudpiercer], dealing extra damage to enemies with high Overdrive costs.
lore:
Captain of the Wood Elf Defense Squad and a masterful archer. Deeply loyal to her kin, she harbors a quiet but unwavering hatred toward the dark elves. Though she lives simply, she often spends her free time alone in the forest, still and focused, using solitude as a form of peace.

"For our people to live peacefully in this forest forever... that is all I desire."

On the battlefield, he would never abandon a single comrade—willing even to take a blow in another's place. Deeply respected by every elf in the defense squad, he is also well-versed in herbal healing, tending to others' wounds after battle while paying no mind to his own.

"The power of the forest will heal our wounds."

Deeply responsible by nature, she always makes one last patrol of the territory alone after a day's work—sustained only by a few elven biscuits. On one such patrol, she discovered the presence of a dark elf assassin and bravely engaged them in combat, ultimately thwarting a surprise attack. For this, she was commended by the queen—an honor she regards as the highest of her life.

She once had a childhood friend—someone she practiced archery with, someone she promised to join the defense force alongside. But on the night of the enlistment ceremony, the dark elves launched a massive attack and her friend was killed in battle. She buried the body with her own hands, yet even now, she still dreams of the times they spent laughing together.

The sudden surge in the dark elves' strength brought about heavy losses to the defense squad. Though she maintains a calm exterior, she quietly blames herself—and her hatred toward the Dark Elves continues to grow. With war looming, she has already steeled herself for the worst.

"For our homeland... for the comrades we've lost... fight until the last moment! Never retreat!"

name: Loki

She marks targets to significantly ignore their Magic Defense using [Curse Blast], and constantly copies and enhances her previously cast skills with [Repeat Performance].
title: Goddess of Trickery
lore: Loki is a god of Asgard born of the giants. Her heritage ensured she was never loved by the gods, yet her authority forced them to bury their resentment. She is like a dual prism—at times a dazzling, cunning figure, and at others a bottomless blaze of chaos.

The gods watched by Loki are pitiful indeed. Unaware, they surrender loyalty, treasures, talents, even their lives under her designs. Those who glimpse the truth rage in fury, yet cannot harm the Goddess of Trickery in the slightest—only deepening their anger.

After the death of Baldr, the God of Light, Loki—burdened with the gods' fury—was imprisoned by Odin. She entered her cage calmly, knowing it was all part of the plan. Loki had long prepared the stage for Ragnarok, and Baldr's death was merely the opening bell. Using the World Tree as her chessboard, she swore to overturn the old order.

As Ragnarok approached, Loki's followers freed her from captivity. She led her army into battle against the gods and perished alongside Heimdall, bringing Ragnarok to its end. With her death, Loki shattered the old order and completed her rebellion. Yet mutual destruction was only one step in her design—she had already slipped quietly beyond the Nine Realms.

No one knows when Loki arrived at Phantasia Mountain, what she seeks, or whether she will bring salvation or ruin. As her golden eyes once again trace the world's veins, the seemingly unbreakable threads of fate woven by ancient prophecy quietly begin to loosen.
quote: Truth is falsehood, black is white~
ssr_quote: Can you tell the difference between truth and lies?

title: Sea Goddess
lore: Poseidon, god of the sea, ruler of oceans, earthquakes, and horses. Legend holds that he gifted humanity its first horse. She is often seen riding across the waves in a golden chariot drawn by white steeds, her presence stirring both awe and fear.

When Poseidon's wrath is unleashed, sea monsters surge from the depths, laying waste to all in their path. With a single sweep of her trident, she conjures towering waves and devastating tsunamis. Yet when she rides her chariot across the sea, the waters grow still and silent beneath her.

"Is it not the sea that determines the shape of the land?"

When Poseidon strikes the rocks with his trident, fresh springs burst forth to nourish the land. Grateful for the bountiful harvests that follow, farmers honor him not only as lord of the sea, but also as a god of abundance.

Poseidon is ambitious and belligerent. He once tried to pull Zeus from his throne and fought with Athena, the goddess of wisdom, for dominion over Athens. However, these attempts ultimately ended in failure.

"I was just horsing around. Why so serious?"

Poseidon, guardian of coastal folk and fishermen, dwells in a resplendent palace beneath the waves. She has long heard the tales of the Ring of Dominion. But in her boundless pride, she believes that even such a power will, in time, be claimed by the sea. To her, nothing escapes the ocean’s grasp. One day, the Ring too shall rest among her trove of sunken treasures.
ssr_quote: I reign supreme over these seas!

Allied Overdrives also build {awakening} stacks that trigger extra casts of [Cascade of Shifting Sands].
title: Black Cat Goddess
lore:
Cleopatra VII, the female pharaoh who ruled Egypt with ruthless authority for many years. Her breathtaking beauty swayed countless hearts and served as a powerful tool in her political arsenal. Brilliant and cunning, she was a master of human insight and deeply versed in arcane arts. Some say her true obsession was the ultimate taboo—the power to bring the dead back to life.

"Even death... must bow before me."

Vicious and ruthless, she regards human life as dust. Like a poisonous flower, she is both beautiful and dangerous. She tests all manner of snake venom on condemned prisoners, seeking the most potent, the most excruciating of toxins. Whispers abound that she poisoned her own husband in just such a manner. Those who dared to gossip were rounded up and fed to her menagerie of savage beasts. Under such rule, none dared defy her...

"To serve as my instrument... is that not an honor in itself?"

On her rise to power, she pledged herself to countless powerful men—only to tear their vows to pieces once they had served their purpose. It seems the queen has never known true love, or so people say as they whisper stories—some true, some not—of her many liaisons. But is the truth really as they imagine...?

People often overlook her brilliance, dazzled by her beauty instead. Fluent in many languages and well-read, she understands the stars and the state of the world alike, her strategic mind and political instincts are razor-sharp, she supports scholars, she fosters learning, but in the end... her achievements are always attributed to the men around her. It hardly matters, though. The power she wields is more than enough to crush anyone foolish enough to underestimate her.

She secretly struck a dark pact with Anubis, mastering forbidden mummification arts and gaining terrifying magical powers. In the shadows, she captured innocent souls, transforming them into mummies and offering them to Anubis's servants. These cursed mummies retain a glimmer of consciousness, their bodies now twisted into weapons that obey only their master's will. Her true motives remain shrouded in mystery...

"I command you—embrace death!"
quote: Do you seek the quicksand secrets?

name: Crassus
summary: A control Mage who uses {punishment} to interfere with enemy Overdrives, stealing cooldown progress and potentially silencing targets. These triggers build Archon's Authority, which strengthens his meteor Overdrive until it can knock enemies back, dispel their buffs, and reduce its own cost. [Pulse Arc] and [Collapse Point] add further dispels, cooldown increases, and Overdrive-cost pressure.
title: Iron-Fisted Regent
lore: Crassus hails from a military aristocratic family in the Nibelgaard Empire, and underwent rigorous training in tactics and leadership from a young age. As the sole heir of her family, she not only continued their martial tradition but also broke the family's military-only focus with her exceptional business acumen, amassing a vast fortune through numerous successful investments. With her unique personal charm and iron-fisted methods, she established a private armed force completely loyal to her, continuously expanding the family's sphere of influence. Ultimately, she ascended to the high position of Imperial Consul through shrewd political strategy and decisive military actions.

Crassus views all interpersonal relationships and military operations as calculable games. This trait was fully displayed during the suppression of the mercenary rebellion: while the council was still debating the cost of quelling the rebellion, she had already used her private resources to form an elite unit and dealt with the rebel leader and its core members through meticulously calculated brutal means—not out of emotion, but as the most effective intimidation strategy after a calm assessment. This operation not only greatly increased her prestige but also made all potential rivals clearly understand the cost of challenging her.

After ascending to the office of Consul, Crassus set about forging a rigorously controlled order. She reformed the military hierarchy, restructured provincial governance, opened new trade routes, and refined the empire's intelligence networks—steadily drawing every mechanism of power into a system she could oversee and command. These sweeping reforms earned her no shortage of enemies, yet they also secured her a decisive ally: Princess Caesar.

During Caesar's campaign, Crassus faced the gravest trial of her political life. The imperial general Pompey rebelled, framing Caesar for treason and driving her into exile.

While stabilizing the empire at home, Crassus mobilized her influence and dispatched the Silver Eagle Knights to search the borderlands. Through relentless effort, Caesar was rescued and reunited with her loyalists. She returned to the imperial capital, where she and Crassus together crushed the rebellion.

On the day of Caesar's ascension, a new policy jointly formulated with Crassus was announced. After that, Crassus cleared all obstacles and was able to fully realize her political ambitions. With her steadfast support, the Nibelgard Empire ushered in a glorious era in the name of Caesar.

"Crassus continued the destiny of the Nibelgard Empire. It was because of her partnership with Empress Caesar that the empire entered its most brilliant era."—"The Decline of Nibelgard"

summary: A unique summoner Mage who forms a [Soulbond] connection with her minion Krul, sharing Attack buffs and healing him by consuming {deathrattle} stacks. She commands Krul to deal heavy area magic damage with [Krul Charge] and attaches delayed-explosion devices with [Bunny Bomb] to enemies or Krul himself for massive area-of-effect damage.
title: Demon Overlord
lore:
Driven by an unquenchable thirst for knowledge, she performed a forbidden ritual of immortality and has lived for centuries in the form of a young girl. A scholar who has read every book and mastered all known wisdom, she now finds the world unbearably dull, with nothing left to learn and nothing new to discover. And so, she wanders, in search of one final mystery—a truth that might still satisfy her boundless mind.

"All theories fade to grey—only the tree of life remains evergreen."

She carries with her a peculiar doll named Krul—a demon in disguise, who feeds on the souls of mortals. Especially fond of devouring the souls of scholars, it forged a pact with Faust, granting her eternal life. The moment she concludes that there is no knowledge left in the world worth learning, Krul will open its maw and consume her soul. In a strange twist of fate, it also serves as her guardian, dispatching all who dare approach before claiming its prize.

For centuries, her only companion has been Krul—a demonic puppet whose voice no one else can hear. Though she possesses near-limitless knowledge, she's never experienced the real world or human society, and still carries the innocence of a girl in her teens. Especially when it comes to basic life skills or hands-on tasks, she considers them beneath her notice—resulting in a level of helplessness that borders on absurd. Day to day, she relies entirely on Krul to take care of her.

Perhaps it was Krul's indulgence that led to her spoiled and willful personality. She looks down on the "fools" she meets on the road, and her arrogance has caused more than a few incidents. Krul, ever weary, tries to rein her in—but like a child in rebellion, she pushes back harder. In her eyes, the world exists to serve her. 

"Hmph... I wouldn't say it's satisfying, but at least it's mildly amusing."

During her travels, she witnessed countless human dramas unfold while uncovering the world's deepest secrets. Yet her hunger for more remained endless. Krul waited patiently for her prey to ripen, knowing full well she would never find true satisfaction... 

"When I reach the summit, only then will I whisper... 'Time, stand still, for you are beautiful.'"

name: Gabriele
summary: A critical-focused Mage who gains immense Critical Hit boosts and restores HP on crits via [Judgment of Mercy]. She becomes untargetable and unleashes heavy area magic damage slashes with [Invictus], heavily enhancing her Overdrive damage by consuming {deathrattle} stacks gained from fallen allies using [Celestial Awakening].
title: Archangel
lore:
One of the archangels of the celestial realm, she serves as Heaven's guardian—proud, unwavering, and blessed by the gods. Untouched by harm, she often grants divine power to righteous warriors and is revered by all who fight for justice. Fiercely opposed to evil, she leads the heavenly host in an eternal war against the forces of Hell, bearing the sacred duty to purge darkness from the world.

"May you forever carry the light of faith and justice in your heart."

When not on the battlefield, she often serves as a messenger—delivering the will of the heavens to humankind. At times, she also acts as the hand of divine judgment, punishing mortal sins on behalf of the higher realm. Throughout history, her presence among mortals has been well documented. She never questions the decrees of the heavens, firmly trusts in her own sense of justice, and accepts the worship and devotion of the faithful with serene grace.

"Keep praying, mortals. So long as your devotion is true, the path ahead shall reveal itself."

As captain of the guard, Gabriele has never once failed in her duty to uphold the sanctity of heaven. Her flawless record has earned her deep trust—even the authority to punish angels who violate divine law. She shows no leniency toward her fellow angels, let alone toward humans. To be cleansed by Gabriele's holy light is, for any mortal, the ultimate proof of a life lived in pious devotion and virtue.

Brave and battle-hardened, Gabriele volunteered to lead Heaven's forces. But the war with Hell dragged on—and in time, some humans fell to temptation. When they sobbed and begged for forgiveness at her feet, Gabriele gave them none... Despite such brutality, she does not doubt the righteousness of her cause.

"The divine show no mercy to those who fall willingly. I shall destroy all who betray justice!"

Though driven by a powerful sense of justice, the Barro Flamefiend and other demons knew just how to provoke her into rash action. As Heaven's forces struggled against these mighty foes, her mounting anxiety left her vulnerable to the Barro Flamefiend's taunts. She charged alone into enemy lines, only to be trapped and captured. Now freed and back in Heaven, she's uncovered the Wild Hunt's shadowy influence and joins her fellow Archangels in plotting their counterattack against Hell.
ssr_quote: I am the herald of the apocalypse!

summary: A debuff-scaling Mage whose damage significantly increases based on the number of debuffs afflicting her target through [Dominion of Pain]. She applies {healing_down} in a large area with [Abyssal Grasp] and continuously drains health from a single target to heal her most injured ally using [Soul Siphon].
title: Demilich
lore:
A sorceress well-versed in both forbidden alchemy and the art of torture, she possesses the rare ability to observe events across other planes. Yet it is the resurrection ritual—said to be known only to her—that places her power on par with the gods. Beneath her alluring appearance lies a warped mind and cruel whims, finding delight in toying with humankind.

"I'll let you in on the secret to rebirth... You've got to learn to take pleasure in the pain."

In ages long past, she was once honored as one of the Vanir. Yet, with treachery in her heart, she sowed the seeds of conflict between the Vanir and the Aesir. Alone, she strode into Asgard, the sacred land of the Aesir, proclaiming that the power of the Vanir reigned supreme over all. Odin hurled his spear at her, and the gods cast her into blazing fire. Still, she rose again—three times slain, three times reborn. And so began the protracted, ruinous war of the gods...

She first studied the forbidden art of resurrection out of a mortal's desperate desire to survive—but the torment she endured twisted her very soul, leaving her obsessed with pain itself. After ascending to godhood, she foresaw the growing rift between the two races and the coming of twilight—and used the gods as pawns, all for the sake of more screams and spilled blood.

"The final cries of dying souls... are the most exquisite symphony the world has to offer."

After the war, she was exiled from the gods and took up residence in a witch's hut, creating spells that brought pain, terror, and death. From time to time, she targets unlucky mortals as sacrifices for her magic. But what she truly craves is not pain—it is another Ragnarok. So when the Black Knight came knocking, she joined the Wild Hunt without a second thought.

Gullveig was first to detect the unstable rifts in space-time at Phantasia Mountain and warn of worlds dangerously merging. She urged the Black Knight to exploit this weakness, reaching out to evil creatures across dimensions. Her dark whispers lured them to Phantasia Mountain, seeking power and alliance with the Wild Hunt to unleash pure devastation.

"Life and death spiral eternally, as souls surge without end... nurturing endless agony."
quote: The age of the gods is long gone!
ssr_quote: Not even the gods can strike me down!

summary: A mechanical Mage who places numerous waiting mechanical orbs around the battlefield, eventually entering the {wild} state to activate all of them simultaneously for massive rapid-fire magic damage via [Directive: Standby]. She deals heavy area damage and recovers Rage based on her orbs using [Directive: Annihilate], while supporting her team by reducing ultimate cooldowns with [Directive: Recharge].
title: Bronze Goddess
lore:
One of the greatest creations of the Bronze Age, Hephaestus forged her bronze body, and Zeus bestowed upon her immortal life with Ambrosia. 
When the giant body faced annihilation, Talos embarked alone, searching for the ichor, seeking a way to restore her complete form.

Once, she guarded Crete through the long ages until the Argonauts arrived. Medea devised a plan to shatter the giant's weak ankle. As the spirit fuid within flowed out through the crack, the bronze giant collapsed with a thunderous crash.
Since then, there have been few records about Talos. Some say she still watches over Crete, eternally unchanging; others say she received the grace of the gods and was reborn.

Whether in the Age of Heroes or the Age of Iron, there is a beauty that Talos never experienced in the Bronze Age. 

"I want... to take a good look at this world... the beauty of the Age of Iron... I want to experience it myself..."

Now, Talos stands atop Phantasia Mountain. She seeks more ambrosia, hoping to use it to restore her original form. 

"I should be the most perfect creation of the gods... I must reclaim the lost ambrosia."
quote: I am a product of the Bronze Age.
ssr_quote: Some see the ugliness of the Iron Age, but I see beauty.

name: Tamamo-no-Mae
summary: A debuff-heavy Mage who steals enemy Magic Defense and Ultimate Damage by applying [Foxfire Bind] stacks with her skills. She unleashes a massive barrage of magic projectiles with [Foxfire Dance], and has a strong chance to inflict {charm} on enemies while gaining {blessing_buff}s using [Nine-Tailed Bewitching].
title: Fox Enchantress
lore:
A peerless beauty who appeared at the end of the Heian period, a Legendary fox spirit whose origins remain a mystery.
Everything began with a chance encounter where the fox spirit met and bonded with a maiden named "Aomi." That pure and untainted kindness made Aomi the primary example for the fox spirit to observe humanity and experience the warmth of emotions.
Aomi was Lucky. Though orphaned and helpless in her youth, she was lovingly adopted by a samurai couple, allowing her to grow into a graceful maiden in peaceful times—free of want, her heart remained untainted. Later, with extraordinary talent and City Romance, she found herself caught in palace intrigues ever since.

As the best friend of the fox spirit, she watched as the once-bright Algae Maiden lost her former radiance and seemed consumed by melancholy, leaving her puzzled as to why someone blessed with everything envied by others could no longer show a genuine smile. The monotonous, dull life in the palace drained the fox spirit's enthusiasm, leading her to frequently sneak out. Each time she returned, she brought back small trinkets from the outside world in an attempt to Dispel her friend's gloom. Over time, the vast world beyond the palace captivated her more and more, and her excursions became longer. Finally, she made a pact with Algae Maiden to temporarily part ways and embark on a journey to witness all the wonders of the mortal realm.

During her journey, the fox spirit witnessed the cycles of human sorrow and joy, finally understanding the unhappiness of the kelpie: it wasn't due to scarcity, but rather the constraints of wealth, luxury, and obligations that caused her to lose her true self. The fox spirit was deeply concerned and immediately set out to help her friend reclaim her happiness.
Upon their reunion, however, the kelpie had already been branded as the 'Charm Sovereign' and imprisoned. When the fox spirit attempted to rescue her, it solidified her reputation as a yokai, drawing the pursuit of the Onmyoji. During their escape, the kelpie broke free from the Spirit Shackles and regained her pure and unburdened smile.

The pursuit of the Onmyoji never ceased, and ultimately they cornered the pair in Nasu Field. The fox spirit fought to the death with all its cultivation power but was outnumbered and fell into disadvantage. At The Edge of Crisis, Aoname unhesitatingly stepped in front of the fox spirit and took the Deathblow. Overcome with grief, the fox spirit lost control and unleashed its demonic power, striking back and killing all the Onmyoji.
In her final moments, Aoname expressed her gratitude, enduring spirit, and love for freedom. The fox spirit buried her with tears, then vanished without a trace from the human world.

Years passed, and a woman dressed in elegant attire with fox ears appeared on Phantasia Mountain. When someone asked about her name, she answered gently, "My name is Tamamo-no-Mae." After inheriting this name, she carried all the memory and emotions of the maiden, embracing her warmth and resilience, and continued her journeys to forge new bonds. Eventually, she settled on Phantasia Mountain, shedding her sorrow and living freely, embodying the life the maiden had always yearned for.
ssr_quote: Some of the rumors about me are actually true~

She unleashes a fire tornado that deals continuous area damage and applies {ignite} with [Brahma's Fire Dance], and possesses a powerful [Nirvanic Rebirth] skill that allows her to survive fatal damage and resurrect from an egg.
title: Four Saints
lore: The Vermilion Bird was born from the power of the stars and stands alongside the Azure Dragon, White Tiger, and Black Tortoise as one of the Four Divine Beasts. For ages, she has guarded the turning of the seasons. She rules the south, often appearing as a girl in red, wielding a flame-forged feather fan and commanding the purest fire, as well as the seven southern constellations.

The Vermilion Bird Deity appears bright and lively, often mistaken for easygoing. In truth, her temperament burns fierce and unyielding. When summer arrives, she becomes the sun itself, driving away all gloom. When evil stirs, a single wave of her feather fan reduces it to ash.

Though she accompanied the Azure Dragon for millennia, the Vermilion Bird never accepted its position as the foremost of the Four Divine Beasts. Each summer solstice, when yang energy peaks, she challenges the Azure Dragon to combat. Their battles often rage from the highest heavens to the vast seas, and during one fierce clash, their true forms were revealed—crimson wings entwined with an azure dragon's shadow, mistaken by mortals as the omen of "dragon and phoenix in harmony." In the end, the Vermilion Bird narrowly lost, a past she least wishes to be remembered.

Though quick-tempered, the Vermilion Bird never wavers in her resolve to protect the mortal world. She favors wise rulers, and when a virtuous emperor rises, her silhouette appears among the southern stars, crimson light stretching for thousands of miles. She often manifests to help righteous kings quell calamities, leaving countless legends of her guidance throughout history.

After attaining enlightenment, the Vermilion Bird found herself at Phantasia Mountain. The land was steeped in both purity and corruption, bearing omens of a wise ruler's rise and signs of looming destruction. She chose to remain. After long observation, she discovered traces of the Azure Dragon and others, and realized that all things were bound by destiny.
quote: Leader of all birds, born of the crimson cave.

name: Yekaterina
summary: A Chill-focused Mage who builds Ice Soul to automatically create Frost Vortexes that damage and slow groups of enemies. [Ice Blast] lowers Magic Defense and becomes stronger inside a vortex, while [Polar Sigil] suppresses the fastest enemy with Attack Speed reduction and {chill}. [Frozen Armor] lets her support allies with shields and Damage Amplification, especially against chilled targets.
title: Queen of the North
lore: Yekaterina II, the Supreme Empress of the North, the Ruler of the Romanov Dynasty, and the only female Ruler in Northern history to be bestowed the title of "the Great," expanded her territories with the might of thunder, forging the golden age of the empire with majesty and strategy. She grew up cherished and expected by her family. All the dramatic changes were frozen in that frigid winter when she was fourteen. The barbarian tribes at the empire's borders suddenly revolted, and her father and brothers led the army to suppress the rebellion, but they never returned to their homeland, forever remaining in that snow-covered winter.

The young Yekaterina was forced to ascend the throne, and she needed to adapt to her new identity in a very short time. Various issues lay before her—unresolved riots, a chaotic court, and the death of her family members. With her intelligence, Yekaterina quickly stabilized the court and seized the core of power, finally allowing her to find time to deal with the murderer of her father and brother.

Her Majesty the Empress personally led the expedition. Under the Siege of strong troops, the tribal forces retreated step by step. Yekaterina led her army in a relentless Pursuit northward. During the decisive battle, the tribal Leader unexpectedly Summoned a massive Blizzard. The young Empress finally understood why her father and brother met their demise here. She became separated from her guards in the snowstorm and ventured into the deepest, coldest part.

In a near-death status, a tremendous surge of magic power erupts from Yekaterina's body—stemming from her mother's lineage, the unique strength of the Ice Witch awakens at this moment. The frigid temperature becomes an extension of her will, the fierce wind her conscious touch, and the flying snow her grace, she becomes the Ice Age itself. Yekaterina's vengeance is completed in only this moment, and from then on, no one can defeat her in the wind and snow.

Yekaterina became a highly skilled Ruler. When the room was filled with nobles arguing incessantly, she could quiet everyone with a single sentence. When an old minister bent down to kiss the back of her hand and looked up, blurting out "Your Majesty," Yekaterina merely nodded slightly, as if she was born to be the sole master of the North.

lore: A beast of the underworld, the hound of hell. It stands watch at the gate, allowing none to leave.
It's said that a honey cake placed in the coffin of the dead is meant to appease Cerberus, the hound who stands watch in the underworld.
The hellhound's three heads drip with venom, each drop laced with deadly poison. When it howls, it spews a foul miasma—its breath a plague upon the living.
As the pet of the Queen of the Underworld, Cerberus represents the absolute authority of the goddess of death. Wherever he stands, the will of Hades follows.
To overcome death, you must first face Cerberus - challenge him with brute force or master the Affirmation of Wisdom!
quote: I'll split you into three pieces.

title: Queen of Egypt
lore:
Cleopatra VII, the female pharaoh who ruled Egypt with ruthless authority for many years. Her breathtaking beauty swayed countless hearts and served as a powerful tool in her political arsenal. Brilliant and cunning, she was a master of human insight and deeply versed in arcane arts. Some say her true obsession was the ultimate taboo—the power to bring the dead back to life.

"Even death... must bow before me."

Vicious and ruthless, she regards human life as dust. Like a poisonous flower, she is both beautiful and dangerous. She tests all manner of snake venom on condemned prisoners, seeking the most potent, the most excruciating of toxins. Whispers abound that she poisoned her own husband in just such a manner. Those who dared to gossip were rounded up and fed to her menagerie of savage beasts. Under such rule, none dared defy her...

"To serve as my instrument... is that not an honor in itself?"

On her rise to power, she pledged herself to countless powerful men—only to tear their vows to pieces once they had served their purpose. It seems the queen has never known true love, or so people say as they whisper stories—some true, some not—of her many liaisons. But is the truth really as they imagine...?

People often overlook her brilliance, dazzled by her beauty instead. Fluent in many languages and well-read, she understands the stars and the state of the world alike, her strategic mind and political instincts are razor-sharp, she supports scholars, she fosters learning, but in the end... her achievements are always attributed to the men around her. It hardly matters, though. The power she wields is more than enough to crush anyone foolish enough to underestimate her.

She secretly struck a dark pact with Anubis, mastering forbidden mummification arts and gaining terrifying magical powers. In the shadows, she captured innocent souls, transforming them into mummies and offering them to Anubis's servants. These cursed mummies retain a glimmer of consciousness, their bodies now twisted into weapons that obey only their master's will. Her true motives remain shrouded in mystery...

"I command you—embrace death!"

She inflicts {magic_defense_down} with [Sanctum of Light] and consistently supports her team by providing {morale} and [Damage Boost] with [Mystic Blessing].
title: Flame Witch
lore: Melina, Child of Flame. When the great wizard Merlin found an infant left on his doorstep, her body wreathed in fire and with no note and no clue to her origin, he took her in and named her after himself. Though he searched for her parents for a long, long time, their identities remain unknown to this day.

Melina has been learning magic from Merlin since she was a child. Her mastery of flame spells was particularly impressive. Merlin once confided to King Arthur that this child would one day surpass him, and was destined to become the next royal wizard.

Until the age of ten, Melina truly believed she was Merlin's granddaughter, and that her parents had gone off to war, never to return. Merlin often wrestled with the decision of whether to reveal the truth about her origins, but when faced with the girl's fiery spirit and radiant smile, he found himself unable to speak.

One day, Merlin told Melina he would be leaving Camelot to journey across the world. He warned her that a ringbearer would soon arrive, and asked her to guide them when the time came. As always, Melina obeyed her teacher's words and waited, filled with quiet anticipation.

Watching the Ringsworn depart, a warm flame ignites in Melina's heart. Growing up sheltered in Camelot, she had only heard tales of adventure from Merlin, who brought back exotic treasures and legends from distant lands. But stories pale against the thrill of discovery - perhaps it's time to take that first brave step into the unknown.
quote: This is... the Grand Flame Burst!

title: Four Seasons Deer Spirit
lore: A young deer newly awakened in human form, taking the shape of a bright-eyed girl. Innocent and carefree, she may be naive to the ways of the world, but her heart is clear and pure. Gifted with the ability to commune with flora, she approaches all things with boundless curiosity and gentle kindness.

When Nanalie first gained consciousness, she didn't know who she was or why she was here. The only thing she remembered was eating sweet Leaves on a giant tree. 

"I guess I need a name first... Nanalie sounds nice! Yup, that's it, I'll be Nanalie from now on!"

She is happy to guide the lost and has helped injured travelers. If you encounter her in the forest, feel free to greet her warmly, as she will respond to you even more enthusiastically. 

"Hello! Are you here to play in the forest too?"

Until now, Nanalie's world had been no larger than this quiet little forest. But passing travelers often spoke of wonders beyond the trees, of strange happenings and legendary heroes. Deep in her heart, Nanalie longed to see the grand capital of the kingdom, and to meet the brave warriors who had slain fearsome dragons.

That day, Nanalie finally mustered the courage to step out of the forest and embark on her journey. But she discovered that the world wasn't always as beautiful as in the stories. Deception, harm, war... This journey was not without its rewards, as Nanalie finally understood that her mission was to protect this forest, this isolated sanctuary.

"I will protect the forest! And everyone in it!"

title: Shadow Elemental
lore:
An elemental being born of darkness, rarely seen by human eyes and often hidden from view. Its presence radiates a dim, ghostly glow that unsettles those nearby. With a brooding nature and distant air, it drifts silently through the world, untouched by light.

"Darkness... is a gentle caress."

Just like Radiant Elementals, Shadow Elementals dwell in their own plane—shifting endlessly between realms until, over time, they take on a human guise. She welcomes the lost and the fallen, those wandering paths shunned by the light. Though her road lies in darkness, it is still a road—still a way forward for those with nowhere else to turn.

The Goddess of Fate seem to favor Radiant Elemental, spreading the brilliance of written destiny wherever she walks. The Shadow Elemental, by contrast, lingers silently in the dark, merely watching the world go by. Perhaps she was never meant to possess beauty or warmth... or perhaps, enduring solitude is its own form of refinement.

To follow her own path and see the world in the darkness, Telperion ultimately chose to leave the Goddess of Fate. After that, her first mission was to guard a sacred spear.

"Everything carries its own purpose—whether it's a blessing or a curse, it's all the same."

When the Ringbearer claimed the Holy Spear and pressed on with the quest, Telperion's duty was complete. Once again, uncertainty clouded her mind. Yet through this haze, a flicker of understanding emerged - what gave the Ringbearer such unwavering resolve to scale the peak?

"In brightness, we lose sight of ourselves. Only in shadow do we truly grasp how brilliant the light can be."

title: Mischievous Imp
lore:
A small lizardman whose appearance tends to divide opinion—some find it cute, others... not so much.

"So you're saying I'm, like... ugly-cute?"

Buck is quite popular among mages, and is often spotted lounging in mage towers and arcane labs. Mages usually use him heat their magical apparatus—though more than one tower has gone up in smoke from a moment's carelessness.

Mages believe the world is composed of four elements—earth, water, air, and fire—each linked to a corresponding elemental spirit. The spirit of fire is known as the salamander. However, Buck is not a true salamander, but rather a replica created by mages.

Perhaps because he's only a replica, Buck's control over fire is far weaker than that of a true salamander. Still, he shares their impulsive, reckless temperament—and regularly leaves his mage master's laboratory in a smoldering mess.
Rather than sending Buck into battle, Mages who summon this familiar spend more time making sure they don't get scorched themselves!

She deals massive area magic damage to both allies and enemies with [Death's Embrace] and scales her Attack whenever allies fall.
title: Wandering Ghost
lore:
A lonely ghost wandering the world in the form of a young girl. She drifts without a home, her memories lost to time—only a lingering sorrow remains. Able to sense approaching tragedies, especially death, she instinctively appears near those fated to die.

"Another tragedy begins... Who shall pass, who shall weep, and who will remember it all?"

Although she has no intention of harming anyone, she is often seen beside those who are about to die, and over time, humans have come to regard her as an ominous presence. To avoid causing panic, she usually stays in sparsely populated forests, but occasionally she still frightens passing travelers. Sometimes, she plays with small animals that are not afraid of her.

"This sorrow... is it too heavy for humans to bear...?"

In life, she was just an ordinary human girl, living a peaceful, uneventful life—until one night, an unknown band of raiders attacked her village, burning, looting, and killing. She watched her parents and friends perish, her cries for help unheard. That pain and longing followed her into the underworld...

Unable to let go of her grief, she returned from death and exacted revenge on those who wronged her. But once the blood settled, and the corpses piled high, only emptiness remained. Her hatred had burned out, but sorrow lingered—and the tears never stopped. Now, she senses pain wherever it exists, drawn ever deeper into death's quiet call...

Driven by pure instinct, she drifted through the mortal realm in a trance. Time slipped past - centuries vanishing like mist. After witnessing countless farewells and final breaths, her numb heart yearned for Redemption, for an end to sorrow, for fear to finally fade...

"Someone... save me... end this Endless suffering and grant me Eternal rest..."

lore: Dwarven Sages are magic-wielders among their kind, and unlike the elves or fairies who favor arcane or nature-based spells, dwarven priests specialize in rune magic.

Rune magic serves many purposes, but dwarven priests have a knack for turning it into a weapon of war. At times, they'll channel runes to bolster their own brawn, becoming living weapons on the battlefield.

"Ditch the staff—go all in with your fists!"

All rune magic originates from Odin's wisdom, and the runes used by Dwarven Sages are no exception. According to dwarf history, Odin once commissioned dwarf craftsmen to forge weapons for the einherjar. As payment, he taught the dwarves rune magic.

Dwarven priests also serve as royal scribes, recording the history of the dwarven kingdom. But more importantly, they keep a ledger of grudges—documenting those who have wronged their people and compiling the names into the infamous Book of Vengeance.

"As long as this book endures, so shall our hatred."

Since the fall of the Dwarven Kingdom, displaced dwarves have scattered across Phantasia Mountain. Though not warriors in the traditional sense, dwarven priests have taken it upon themselves to protect their people—standing by the homeless and weary, using rune magic to shield them from harm.

name: Pharaoh
summary: A lifesteal Mage who scales his Attack permanently as allies fall on the battlefield via {shroud}. He drains the life of a single target over time to restore his own health with [Bloodsuck] and deals area magic damage around a target using [Toxic Touch].
lore: The Pharaoh was the ruler of ancient Egypt, holding supreme authority over the military, government, law, and religion. Claiming to be the son of the Sun Goddess, the Pharaoh was regarded as both the divine representative and living embodiment of the gods on earth.

The pharaoh stands at the pinnacle of the pyramid of power, offering prayers to the gods in exchange for might. The people's devotion borders on madness, and even uttering his name conjures an irresistible force.

"Kiss the dirt beneath my feet, mortal."

Pharaohs often wore the "Nemes" headdress and carried various scepters. The "Heka" crook symbolized rulership, the "Was" scepter stood for unification, and the "Nekhakha" flail was a symbol carried only by pharaohs who had passed into the afterlife.

After death, pharaohs are made into mummies and sealed in chambers deep within their pyramids. To prevent grave robbers from disturbing their rest, they command their servants to construct deadly traps—ensuring peace until the day their soul returns.

"Whoever dares disturb a pharaoh's slumber shall feel the wings of death upon their neck."

People call the strange phenomena that occur after entering the Pharaoh's tomb the Pharaoh's Curse. These mysterious forces are believed to torment and eventually destroy any intruder who dares disturb the sacred site.

"Any who enters this tomb with an impure heart... I will crush their neck as one would a bird."
